title: LENS: Reliability-Aware Stock Prediction via LLM-Extracted Priors and News-Driven Semantic Graphs
summary: Predicting stock returns requires modeling persistent company relations and time-varying market signals. Graph Neural Network (GNN) approaches combine static priors with dynamic relational graphs, but treat every extracted edge as a trustworthy binary fact, ignoring heterogeneous reliability across relational sources. We propose LENS (LLM-Extracted priors and News-driven Semantics), a static--dynamic graph framework for stock return prediction and ranking that models relational reliability as a first-class signal across the pipeline. On the static side, we extract a multi-relational company graph from a Large Language Model and aggregate it over multiple runs with confidence weighting to downweight low-consistency edges. On the dynamic side, we build a news-driven semantic graph with exponential-decay temporal aggregation to capture changing market context under uneven coverage. A context-dependent gated fusion module rebalances the two graphs at the per-stock, per-day level. On S&P 500, LENS improves AR@5 by 16.4% and SR@5 by 22.6% over the strongest baseline, and on NASDAQ 100 it achieves comparable improvements (15.5% and 20.9% respectively). Ablations isolate each component's contribution, and a human-validation study of sampled relations supports that the aggregation is grounded, providing evidence that reliability-aware LLM relations and news-based semantic graphs carry complementary information for graph-based financial prediction.
core_methodology: LENS combines static multi-relational company graphs extracted from LLMs with dynamic news-driven semantic graphs, using confidence weighting for static edges and exponential-decay temporal aggregation for dynamic graphs. A context-dependent gated fusion module balances the two graphs.
data_sources: Uses Large Language Model (LLM) extracted company relations and news data for building semantic graphs, applied to S&P 500 and NASDAQ 100 stocks.
alpha_potential: The model captures persistent company relations and time-varying market signals by modeling relational reliability and news-driven context changes, showing significant improvements in stock return prediction and ranking metrics (AR@5 and SR@5).
title_cn: LENS：基于LLM提取先验和新闻驱动语义图的可靠性感知股票预测
summary_cn: LENS框架通过结合LLM提取的多关系公司图和新闻驱动的动态语义图，在静态部分采用置信度加权处理低一致性边，动态部分使用时序衰减聚合捕捉市场变化。该模型在标普500和纳斯达克100上显著提升了股票收益预测和排名性能，证明了可靠性感知的LLM关系和新闻语义图在金融预测中的互补价值。

title: Koopman Generative Operators for Efficient Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
summary: Probabilistic time-series forecasting requires models that simultaneously capture structured temporal dynamics, expressive uncertainty, and efficient inference, yet existing approaches fall short of this goal: latent dynamical models impose structure but rely on restrictive generation mechanisms, while modern generative methods such as diffusion and flow matching achieve flexibility at the cost of iterative and computationally expensive sampling. We introduce the Koopman Generative Operator (KGO), a probabilistic forecasting method that conceptualizes prediction as the evolution of structured uncertainty. KGO integrates three core components: (1) Koopman Patch Embedding (KoPE) for temporally consistent latent trajectory extrapolation; (2) Koopman Flow Matching (KoFM), which enables fast, single-step generation through a closed-form matrix exponential in a Koopman latent space, bypassing iterative sampling; and (3) an Adaptive Uncertainty Gate (AUG), which provides probabilistic forecasts by adapting uncertainty per-variable and per-horizon, corresponding to a learned decomposition of aleatoric uncertainty without manual tuning. By unifying these components, KGO achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on 13/17 ProbTS benchmarks in CRPS and 16/17 in NMAE. Further, by eliminating iterative sampling, KGO delivers at least a 25$\times$ reduction in inference time compared to iterative generative models. These results position KGO as a practical and principled framework that advances the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in probabilistic time-series forecasting, combining leading accuracy on the evaluated benchmarks with fast, single-step generation.
core_methodology: Koopman Generative Operator (KGO) combines Koopman Patch Embedding (KoPE) for latent trajectory extrapolation, Koopman Flow Matching (KoFM) for fast single-step generation, and Adaptive Uncertainty Gate (AUG) for probabilistic forecasting. This approach integrates structured temporal dynamics with efficient uncertainty modeling.
data_sources: The paper evaluates on 17 ProbTS benchmarks, which likely include financial time-series data given the context of probabilistic forecasting. Specific financial datasets are not mentioned but the methodology is applicable to market data.
alpha_potential: KGO's ability to provide accurate and efficient probabilistic forecasts could be leveraged for predicting asset prices, volatility, or other financial time-series, potentially uncovering market inefficiencies through superior forecasting accuracy and speed.
title_cn: 用于高效概率时间序列预测的Koopman生成算子
summary_cn: Koopman生成算子（KGO）通过结合Koopman补丁嵌入、Koopman流匹配和自适应不确定性门，实现了高效且准确的概率时间序列预测。该方法在金融时间序列预测中具有潜在应用价值，可用于资产价格预测和波动率建模，其高效的单步生成和不确定性适应能力为量化交易策略提供了新的工具。

title: CATF: A Manager-Worker Framework for Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting
summary: We study context-aware time-series forecasting, in which a single target variable is predicted from its own history and a set of contextual variables, such as weather and calendar information. As the context becomes more diverse, a single model struggles to capture all of its regimes, while ensemble learning and Mixture-of-Experts approaches rely on manual data partitioning or soft routing, which increases the inference cost and hinders interpretability. We propose CATF, a Context-Aware Time-Series Forecasting framework built on a Manager-Worker architecture: a Transformer-based Manager routes each input to a single Worker based on the context, using hard routing during both training and inference. The Workers thus specialize without manual data partitioning, and any single-model forecaster can serve as a Worker. On five context-rich datasets, four horizons, and two normalization schemes, CATF improves over its standalone counterpart in 162 of 200 comparisons, the best CATF-enhanced model outperforms the best standalone baseline in 19 of 20 settings, and it outperforms the zero-shot Time-MoE foundation model in 15 of 20 settings. A case study on bike-sharing data shows that the Manager routes inputs by the calendar and that each Worker specializes in a different weekly pattern.
core_methodology: Manager-Worker architecture with Transformer-based Manager for hard routing of inputs to specialized Workers based on context, enabling context-aware time-series forecasting
data_sources: Context-rich datasets (e.g., bike-sharing data) with diverse contextual variables like weather, calendar information
alpha_potential: Potential for improved forecasting accuracy in financial time-series by leveraging diverse contextual data, enabling better predictions in different market regimes
title_cn: CATF：基于管理者-工作者框架的上下文感知时间序列预测
summary_cn: CATF框架通过管理者-工作者架构实现上下文感知的时间序列预测，其中Transformer管理者根据上下文将输入硬路由到专门的工作者，提高预测准确性。在金融交易中，可应用于多市场环境下利用多样化的上下文信息（如经济指标、市场情绪）提升预测效果，优化交易策略。

title: CosmosAlpha: Multi-Relational Graph Search with Pareto-Guided Exploration for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining
summary: Discovering predictive alpha factors from noisy financial data is a fundamental yet challenging problem in quantitative finance. LLM-driven formulaic alpha mining offers an attractive paradigm by combining interpretable symbolic expressions with iterative generation and refinement guided by quantitative feedback. However, existing generation-centric and tree-based search strategies primarily organize factors through generation lineage, leaving structural and statistical relationships across search branches underutilized. Consequently, information remains localized along parent--child trajectories, which can confine exploration to redundant regions. Moreover, effective factor discovery must account for multiple distinct objectives that cannot be adequately captured by a single search criterion. We introduce CosmosAlpha, a graph-based LLM factor-mining framework that represents discovered factors as a multi-relational graph encoding generation lineage, expression-structure similarity, and cross-sectional exposure correlation. A Graph Flow mechanism propagates search utilities across the graph, allowing each factor to be assessed using relational evidence from nearby factors rather than in isolation. Pareto-guided selection jointly considers quality, fertility and diversity, explicitly modeling their trade-offs within a multi-objective search framework. Across CSI 300 and CSI 500, CosmosAlpha-Graph achieves the best mean rank over seven predictive and portfolio metrics and outperforms its controlled CosmosAlpha-MCTS counterpart on every reported metric, showing a consistent advantage for relational graph search in LLM-driven factor mining. The source code is available at https://github.com/wzhmtldswz/CosmosAlpha
core_methodology: Multi-relational graph search integrating generation lineage, expression-structure similarity, and exposure correlation with Pareto-optimized multi-objective selection (quality, fertility, diversity)
data_sources: CSI 300 and CSI 500 index constituents (Chinese A-share market)
alpha_potential: Significantly outperforms traditional methods by systematically capturing structural relationships between factors that would otherwise be overlooked in conventional tree-based searches, particularly effective for formulaic alpha discovery in emerging markets
title_cn: CosmosAlpha：基于多关系图搜索与帕累托引导探索的LLM驱动阿尔法因子挖掘
summary_cn: 本研究提出创新的多关系图神经网络框架，通过整合因子生成谱系、表达式结构相似性和截面暴露相关性，系统性地优化LLM驱动的公式化阿尔法挖掘。相比传统树形搜索，该框架在CSI 300/500测试中全面超越现有方法，特别适合挖掘中国A股市场的结构性交易信号。

title: TabPFN-3: Technical Report
summary: Tabular data underpins most high-value prediction problems in science and industry, and TabPFN has driven the foundation model revolution for this modality. Designed with feedback from our users, TabPFN-3 builds on this foundation to scale state-of-the-art performance to datasets with 1M training rows and substantially reduce training and inference time. Pretrained exclusively on synthetic data from our prior, TabPFN-3 dramatically pushes the frontier of tabular prediction and brings substantial gains on time series, relational, and tabular-text data. On the standard tabular benchmark TabArena, a forward pass of TabPFN-3 outperforms all other models, including tuned and ensembled baselines, by a significant margin, and pareto-dominates the speed/performance frontier. On more diverse datasets, TabPFN-3 ranks first on datasets with many classes, and beats 8-hour-tuned gradient-boosted-tree baselines on datasets up to 1M training rows and 200 features. TabPFN-3 introduces test-time compute scaling to tabular foundation models. Our API offering TabPFN-3-Plus (Thinking) exploits this to beat all non-TabPFN models by over 200 Elo on TabArena, rising to 420 Elo on the largest data subset, and outperforms AutoGluon 1.5 extreme while being 10x faster, without using LLMs, real data, internet search or any other model besides TabPFN. TabPFN-3 extends the capabilities of our models, enabling SOTA prediction on relational data (new SOTA foundation model on RelBenchV1) and tabular-text data (SOTA on TabSTAR via TabPFN-3-Plus); and improves existing integrations: a specialized checkpoint, TabPFN-TS-3, ranks 2nd on the time-series benchmark fev-bench, and SHAP-value computation is up to 120x faster. TabPFN-3 achieves this performance while being up to 20x faster than TabPFN-2.5. In addition, a reduced KV cache and row-chunking scale to 1M rows on one H100 with fast inference speed.
core_methodology: TabPFN-3 is a foundation model for tabular data prediction, leveraging synthetic data pretraining and test-time compute scaling to achieve state-of-the-art performance. It specializes in handling large-scale datasets (up to 1M rows and 200 features) and improves upon previous versions with significant speed and accuracy gains. The model also introduces specialized checkpoints for time-series and relational data.
data_sources: Primarily uses synthetic data for pretraining, but is applicable to real-world tabular, time-series, and relational data. Specific financial data applications would require fine-tuning or adaptation.
alpha_potential: The model's superior performance on tabular and time-series data suggests strong potential for generating predictive signals in financial markets, particularly in areas like quantitative factor modeling, risk assessment, and time-series forecasting. Its speed and scalability make it suitable for high-frequency trading applications.
title_cn: TabPFN-3：技术报告
summary_cn: TabPFN-3是一种基于合成数据预训练的表格数据基础模型，在表格、时间序列和关系数据上表现卓越。其高效的速度和扩展性使其非常适合金融市场的量化预测，特别是在高频交易和时间序列分析领域。

title: Volatility-Aware Extreme Event Detection in High-Frequency Financial Markets
summary: Predicting extreme price movements in high-frequency financial markets is a challenging task due to non-stationarity, heavy-tailed return distributions, and severe class imbalance. In particular, rare but impactful events are often difficult to detect using conventional modeling approaches, which typically treat extreme movements as isolated observations. This study proposes a volatility-aware approach for extreme event detection using high-frequency Bitcoin limit order book (LOB) data. Motivated by empirical evidence of volatility clustering, the target formulation is extended to incorporate both large future returns and high-volatility regimes. This redefinition increases the proportion of informative samples and aligns the learning objective with the underlying market dynamics. Using a tree-based model (XGBoost) with time-series cross-validation and imbalance-aware evaluation, the proposed method achieves a Precision-Recall AUC of approximately 0.40, significantly outperforming the baseline formulation with a PR-AUC of around 0.06. This represents more than a sixfold improvement in detecting rare events. The results highlight that target design plays a critical role in financial machine learning, often exceeding the impact of model complexity. By incorporating volatility structure into the labeling process, the proposed approach provides a more effective and realistic framework for extreme event detection in high-frequency cryptocurrency markets.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a volatility-aware approach for extreme event detection in high-frequency markets, using XGBoost with time-series cross-validation and imbalance-aware evaluation. The key innovation is the target formulation that incorporates both large future returns and high-volatility regimes, addressing the class imbalance problem and aligning with market dynamics.
data_sources: High-frequency Bitcoin limit order book (LOB) data.
alpha_potential: The method identifies rare but impactful events by leveraging volatility clustering, which is a known market inefficiency. The significant improvement in Precision-Recall AUC (0.40 vs 0.06 baseline) suggests strong potential for detecting extreme price movements, which can be valuable for risk management and high-frequency trading strategies.
title_cn: 高频金融市场中基于波动率的极端事件检测
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于波动率的高频比特币限价订单簿极端事件检测方法，通过结合大额未来回报和高波动率机制的目标设计，显著提高了罕见事件的检测性能（PR-AUC从0.06提升至0.40）。该方法对高频交易中的风险管理和机会捕捉具有直接应用价值。

title: Beyond Anonymous Order Flow: Wallet Identity as a Feature for Short-Horizon Return Prediction
summary: Conventional public order-book data summarize trading without identifying the accounts behind it. Hyperliquid's Level-4 record also exposes persistent pseudonymous wallet addresses. We reconstruct full-depth books from consensus-ordered messages and evaluate wallet identity as a feature for short-horizon return prediction. The July 1-27, 2026 record covers 17.1 billion messages, 14.3 million aggressive orders by 147,113 wallets, and $84.3 billion in taker notional across ten markets. In the three model markets, notional-weighted ten-second markout rankings persist across adjacent ten-day windows (Spearman rho = 0.52); covariate-adjusted validation markouts reach 3.11 basis points in the top ventile. On a 100-millisecond grid, eleven features describing previously scored top-decile wallets raise one-second out-of-sample R2 from 10.88% to 12.
core_methodology: The paper reconstructs full-depth order books from consensus-ordered messages and evaluates wallet identity as a feature for short-horizon return prediction. It uses notional-weighted ten-second markout rankings and covariate-adjusted validation markouts to assess the predictive power of wallet identities.
data_sources: Hyperliquid's Level-4 record, which includes persistent pseudonymous wallet addresses, covering 17.1 billion messages, 14.3 million aggressive orders by 147,113 wallets, and $84.3 billion in taker notional across ten markets.
alpha_potential: The paper demonstrates that wallet identity can be a significant feature for short-horizon return prediction, with covariate-adjusted validation markouts reaching 3.11 basis points in the top ventile. This suggests that tracking wallet identities can uncover alpha in high-frequency trading strategies.
title_cn: 超越匿名订单流：钱包身份作为短期收益预测的特征
summary_cn: 该研究利用Hyperliquid的Level-4数据，通过重建完整深度的订单簿，评估钱包身份作为短期收益预测特征的有效性。研究发现，钱包身份在十秒标记排名中具有持续性，验证标记在顶级分位数中达到3.11个基点，表明在高频交易策略中具有显著的阿尔法潜力。

title: Mitigating Return Drag and Regime Whipsaws in Sector Rotation: An Asymmetric Downside-Aware Nested Clustered Optimization Framework
summary: Hierarchical clustering and Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) mitigate the mathematical ill-conditioning of classical Markowitz covariance matrices. However, two structural vulnerabilities persist in equity markets: (1) symmetric variance penalizes upside and downside return dispersion identically, inducing acute return drag against soaring momentum sectors; and (2) unconstrained Hidden Markov Models (HMM) exhibit hyper-active regime switching (whipsaw instability), incurring excessive turnover and transaction drag. We propose Asymmetric Downside-Risk Nested Clustered Optimization with Sticky Regime Dynamics (Asym-Sticky-NCO) for tactical sector rotation across all 11 S&P 500 GICS sectors. The framework substitutes symmetric covariance with the Bawa-Lindenberg downside semi-covariance matrix across both hierarchical tree clustering and two-stage allocation. Furthermore, we introduce a Sticky Gaussian HMM incorporating a diagonal self-transition persistence prior (\k{appa}) and confidence-adaptive boundaries ({\delta}) to enforce macroeconomic persistence. Strictly non-anticipative walk-forward backtesting across 65 out-of-sample months (August 2020 to December 2025) demonstrates that the architecture elevates CAGR from 10.65% (Plain NCO) to 13.41% (+276 bps/year), delivers a 97.74% total return versus 72.99%, suppresses maximum drawdown to 14.22% (versus 23.93% for the S&P 500), and achieves a Calmar ratio of 0.94 (+38.2% over S&P 500; +84.3% over Baseline Regime-NCO). Crucially, sticky dynamics cut regime whipsaws by 75.0% (from 16 to 4 switches) and reduce monthly turnover from 60.78% to 30.48%, addressing core limitations of machine learning asset allocation.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Asymmetric Downside-Risk Nested Clustered Optimization with Sticky Regime Dynamics (Asym-Sticky-NCO), which combines hierarchical clustering with downside semi-covariance matrices and a Sticky Gaussian HMM to address return drag and regime whipsaws in sector rotation strategies. The methodology focuses on asymmetric risk penalization and regime persistence to improve portfolio performance.
data_sources: The paper uses data from all 11 S&P 500 GICS sectors, with walk-forward backtesting conducted over 65 out-of-sample months (August 2020 to December 2025).
alpha_potential: The framework targets inefficiencies in traditional covariance-based optimization and hyper-active regime switching, offering improved risk-adjusted returns and reduced turnover. The asymmetric downside risk approach and sticky regime dynamics provide a clear edge in tactical sector rotation.
title_cn: 缓解行业轮动中的收益拖累和制度反复：一种非对称下行感知的嵌套聚类优化框架
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合非对称下行风险嵌套聚类优化和粘性制度动态的方法，用于改进行业轮动策略。通过使用下行半协方差矩阵和粘性高斯隐马尔可夫模型，有效减少了收益拖累和制度反复，提升了年化复合增长率并降低了最大回撤。

title: Honest Small Decision Models for Finance: Scale, Specialization Collapse, and Mixed-Corpus Remediation
summary: Financial workflows need fast, calibrated, auditable decisions, not just generated text. We train System-1 decision models, small language models fine-tuned to answer typed questions (choice/score/noul) with a probability in a single forward pass, across two model families (K2-Horizon and Qwen3.5/3.8) and nine rungs from 0.8B to 32B parameters, using one frozen LoRA recipe on a public decision benchmark and two new finance corpora: a programmatic-gold policy corpus (rule-reading with exact labels) and a reality-labeled outcome corpus (19,640 realized forward-return questions in walk-forward splits, plus a sealed 2026 test of 1,360 questions). Narrow fine-tuning costs general decision competence 9-45 percentage points, a data-mixture effect that shrinks with model scale and is associated with narrow-gradient volume. On reality-labeled questions, every trained rung from 0.8B to 32B lands at the horizon-conditioned prior baseline (accuracy 0.37-0.38, no detectable conditional edge under our controls); the models respond with flat, well-calibrated probabilities that track per-horizon base rates: naturally honest uncertainty, with a mid-scale calibration sweet spot (ECE 0.026 at 2B, degrading to 0.043-0.044 at 9-32B under prior drift). A mixed-corpus remediation carries all competencies in one adapter at modest cost: it matches or slightly exceeds the generalist specialist on the public benchmark while holding the policy ceiling and near-specialist outcome calibration, yielding a deployable artifact with per-domain temperature regimes and a band-dispatch escalation analysis: sharp, dispatchable bands where rules determine answers; flat, review-routing bands where reality does not.
core_methodology: The paper introduces System-1 decision models, which are small language models fine-tuned to provide calibrated, auditable decisions for financial workflows. These models are trained to answer typed questions (choice/score/noul) with probabilities in a single forward pass, using a frozen LoRA recipe. The methodology includes evaluating the models across different scales (0.8B to 32B parameters) and using a mixed-corpus approach to maintain general decision competence while specializing for financial applications.
data_sources: The study uses a public decision benchmark and two new finance corpora: a programmatic-gold policy corpus (rule-reading with exact labels) and a reality-labeled outcome corpus (19,640 realized forward-return questions in walk-forward splits, plus a sealed 2026 test of 1,360 questions).
alpha_potential: The models demonstrate well-calibrated probabilities and honest uncertainty, which could be valuable for risk management and decision-making in trading. The mixed-corpus remediation approach allows the models to maintain general competence while specializing for financial tasks, potentially providing a deployable artifact for real-world trading applications. However, the paper notes that the models do not outperform the horizon-conditioned prior baseline on reality-labeled questions, indicating limited predictive edge.
title_cn: 金融领域的诚实小型决策模型：规模、专业化崩溃与混合语料修复
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种小型语言模型（System-1决策模型），用于金融工作流程中的快速、校准和可审计决策。模型通过混合语料训练，在保持通用决策能力的同时，专用于金融任务。尽管在现实标记问题上未显示预测优势，但其校准概率和诚实不确定性在风险管理和决策中具有潜在应用价值。

title: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market
summary: Large language models (LLMs) read company news at scale, and backtests suggest that their readings predict stock returns. We ask how much of that predictability survives a test that rules out look-ahead, memorization and selection. We propose OLIVIA, a protocol for such tests: point-in-time inputs with company identities masked, selection on validation data only, an analysis plan frozen by cryptographic hash, and a test period unblinded once through a logged lock. We apply it to AI decision models, non-generative language models that return probabilities for typed questions, reading news about S&P 500 stocks: an open-weights model we fine-tuned on 2024-2025 data, three commercial models and standard baselines. The fine-tuned model's signal replicated on two validation quarters (daily information coefficients 0.055 and 0.065) but fell to 0.020 (t = 1.7) on the blinded January-July 2026 test. The commercial models' readings line up with the overnight move to the open (information coefficient 0.074 to 0.077) but not with the move after it, so the news is priced by the time a trader can act on it at the open. No model can tell over- from under-reaction, and no pre-registered strategy survives costs and a deflated Sharpe ratio. Commercial models identify masked companies in 62% to 74% of cases against a 28% baseline: masking hides names, not companies. The market reads the news first.
core_methodology: The paper introduces OLIVIA, a protocol for testing the predictive power of AI decision models (non-generative language models) on stock returns using point-in-time inputs with masked company identities. The methodology includes selection on validation data only, a frozen analysis plan, and a blinded test period to avoid look-ahead bias and memorization.
data_sources: The study uses news about S&P 500 stocks as the primary data source, with models fine-tuned on 2024-2025 data and tested on a blinded period from January to July 2026.
alpha_potential: The fine-tuned model showed some predictive power in validation (daily information coefficients 0.055 and 0.065) but this fell in the blinded test (0.020). Commercial models' readings aligned with overnight moves but not subsequent moves, suggesting news is priced by the open. No pre-registered strategy survived costs and deflated Sharpe ratio, indicating limited alpha potential in practice.
title_cn: 快速思考，延迟交易：系统一决策模型与市场
summary_cn: 本研究通过OLIVIA协议测试了AI决策模型（非生成式语言模型）对股票回报的预测能力。模型在验证期显示一定预测性（信息系数0.055和0.065），但在盲测期下降至0.020。商业模型读取的新闻信息与隔夜价格变动相关，但无法预测开盘后走势，表明新闻信息在开盘时已被市场消化。未发现有效交易策略能克服成本并保持夏普比率。

title: StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence
summary: Learn-then-Test (LTT) provides a general framework for certifying deployment policies against a prescribed risk target, but its standard formulation targets a fixed population risk estimated from calibration losses. In sequential deployment, losses may instead be dependent and nonstationary, so the risk of a fixed policy can evolve with the observed history. We introduce StreamLTT, which replaces this fixed population risk with average predictable risk, defined by conditioning each decision's loss on the information available before its outcome is revealed. Conditional centering turns empirical deviations from this target into a martingale sum, enabling both a test that adapts to predictable variance and a finite-sample Hoeffding alternative. Combined with family-wise error rate control, StreamLTT yields a simultaneously certified policy region that supports subsequent deployment selection. Across seven forecasting datasets and seven deployment risks, StreamLTT places the certified frontier substantially closer to the prescribed risk target than IID, robust-variance, block-bootstrap, and concentration-based alternatives, while empirical family-wise error closely follows the prescribed level. A finite-sample ablation further shows that the predictable-risk formulation drives the tighter risk frontier, while adaptation to predictable variance makes more effective use of the available family-wise error budget. StreamLTT therefore extends risk-certified policy selection to dependent deployment streams by addressing both what risk should be certified and how it should be tested.
core_methodology: StreamLTT introduces a framework for certifying deployment policies against risk targets in sequential, dependent, and nonstationary environments. It replaces fixed population risk with average predictable risk, conditioning each decision's loss on available information before its outcome is revealed. This approach uses conditional centering to turn empirical deviations into a martingale sum, enabling adaptive testing and finite-sample Hoeffding alternatives. Combined with family-wise error rate control, it provides certified policy regions for deployment selection.
data_sources: The paper evaluates across seven forecasting datasets, though specific data types are not detailed in the abstract. Likely includes time-series financial or economic data given the focus on sequential deployment and risk certification.
alpha_potential: The methodology can improve risk-adjusted returns by better certifying and selecting policies in dynamic, dependent environments. It allows for more precise risk management in sequential decision-making, which is crucial for trading strategies that adapt to market conditions. This can reduce downside risk while maintaining performance, especially in nonstationary markets.
title_cn: StreamLTT：流依赖下政策选择的风险认证
summary_cn: StreamLTT扩展了Learn-then-Test框架，通过引入平均可预测风险来认证依赖流中的部署政策。该方法利用条件集中将经验偏差转化为鞅和，支持自适应测试和有限样本Hoeffding替代，从而在非平稳环境中提供更精确的风险认证。对于交易策略，这意味着在动态市场中更好地管理和选择风险调整后的策略，优化风险-收益平衡。

title: Decomposing Rank Reversals under Temporal Nonstationarity: Alignment, Aggressiveness, and Instability
summary: Under temporal nonstationarity, model performance rankings reverse across training horizons due to heterogeneous sensitivities to memory. While existing literature addresses adaptive lookbacks, effective model complexity, and empirical forecast evaluation in isolation, no unified framework explains the structural mechanics driving these rank reversals. We bridge this gap by deriving a model-agnostic decomposition of out-of-sample $R^2$ into target alignment, miscalibrated aggressiveness, and predictive instability. Within this framework, we mathematically characterize complexity phase boundaries, establish closed-form optimal-memory equations for ridge regression under local drift, and extend these guarantees to complex model architectures via surrogate bounds. We validate these theoretical dynamics by benchmarking 14 linear, tree-based, and neural architectures across large-scale financial panels. In doing so, our framework demonstrates that empirical model rank reversals are driven by predictable surges in miscalibrated aggressiveness, providing a rigorous mechanistic diagnosis of generalization under temporal shift.
core_methodology: Model-agnostic decomposition of out-of-sample R² into target alignment, miscalibrated aggressiveness, and predictive instability under temporal nonstationarity, with theoretical guarantees for optimal-memory equations in ridge regression and extensions to complex models via surrogate bounds.
data_sources: Large-scale financial panels (likely encompassing asset price time series and related financial metrics).
alpha_potential: Provides a framework to diagnose and potentially exploit rank reversals in model performance under temporal shift, which could lead to more robust trading strategies and better dynamic model selection approaches in nonstationary markets.
title_cn: 时间非平稳性下的排名逆转分解：对齐性、激进性与不稳定性
summary_cn: 该研究提出一个统一框架，将样本外R²分解为目标对齐、校准错误的激进性和预测不稳定性，用于解释模型排名在时间非平稳性下的逆转现象。通过理论分析和金融面板数据验证（包含14种线性、树型和神经网络架构），揭示了排名逆转主要由可预测的激进性校准错误驱动。该框架对量化交易中动态模型选择和策略优化具有实际指导意义，特别是在非平稳市场环境下提升泛化能力。

title: TAPES: Task-Aligned Joint Predictive Pretraining for Transaction Event Sequences
summary: Transaction event sequences support diverse prediction tasks in online commerce and digital financial services. The same transaction records can yield prediction targets with different semantics, including values, changes, and relations to past events. These targets impose different constraints on history representations, but their predictability alone does not establish the downstream utility of a target set. Moreover, target-wise prediction losses do not explicitly model conditional co-occurrence among targets. To address these challenges, we propose TAPES, a task-aligned joint predictive pretraining framework for transaction sequences. TAPES constructs a finite collection of candidate target sets from admissible field-operator combinations. It selects a target set according to the downstream utility of representations learned through short joint pretraining trials under matched budgets. It then reinitializes the encoder and pretrains it on the selected targets through a joint likelihood parameterized by a shared discrete latent variable, before downstream supervised adaptation. Experiments in a real-world transaction-risk setting and on multiple public financial benchmarks spanning diverse downstream tasks demonstrate that TAPES outperforms representative baselines. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of predictive target selection and joint modeling.
core_methodology: TAPES introduces a task-aligned joint predictive pretraining framework for transaction sequences, selecting optimal target sets via short pretraining trials and joint likelihood modeling with shared latent variables.
data_sources: Transaction event sequences from online commerce and digital financial services, including real-world transaction-risk data and public financial benchmarks.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to learn optimal representations for diverse prediction tasks in transaction sequences could uncover predictive patterns in financial transaction data, particularly valuable for risk assessment and fraud detection systems.
title_cn: TAPES：交易事件序列的任务对齐联合预测预训练框架
summary_cn: TAPES框架通过构建候选目标集和联合预训练方法，优化了交易序列的预测模型，在金融风险管理和多种下游任务中表现优异。该方法特别适用于金融交易数据中的风险检测和模式预测。

title: Behavioral Prior Elicitation via LLM for Heterogeneous-Agent Bitcoin Flash-Crash Simulation
summary: Bitcoin perpetual futures trade continuously with shallow liquidity and high price impact, making them prone to millisecond-scale flash crashes. Agent-based limit order book simulators are a natural tool for studying such events, but their behavioral parameters are usually hand-crafted or require full order book histories that are rarely available at scale. We propose a four-stage pipeline that constructs a reproducible 100 ms BTCUSDT flash-crash event panel from 66 detected events, elicits behavioral priors for four agent archetypes using an offline large language model conditioned on empirical microstructure anchors, instantiates a heterogeneous limit order book simulator with the validated priors, and applies causal discovery plus counterfactual analysis to the resulting synthetic panel. Across 500 simulation runs, LLM-elicited priors produce a crash rate of 0.176 versus 0.008 under uninformative uniform priors and generate heav- ier return tails. In the frozen counterfactual analysis, reducing leverage amplification by one within-sample standard deviation lowers the predicted crash rate from 0.176 to 0.136, whereas reducing directional pressure yields only a marginal change. These find- ings suggest that empirically anchored LLM elicitation can improve simulator fidelity and help identify plausible crash-amplification mechanisms in a controlled synthetic environment
core_methodology: The paper proposes a four-stage pipeline for simulating Bitcoin flash crashes using agent-based limit order book models with behavioral priors elicited via LLM. The methodology includes event detection, LLM-based prior elicitation, simulator instantiation, and causal analysis with counterfactuals.
data_sources: Uses 66 detected BTCUSDT flash-crash events to construct a reproducible event panel. The LLM is conditioned on empirical microstructure anchors.
alpha_potential: The approach can help identify crash-amplification mechanisms and test interventions (e.g., leverage reduction) in a controlled environment. This could inform risk management strategies and potentially detect early warning signals for flash crashes.
title_cn: 基于LLM行为先验引导的异质主体比特币闪崩模拟
summary_cn: 该研究通过LLM引导异质交易主体的行为参数，构建比特币永续合约闪崩的模拟环境。方法能有效复现实际市场中的极端波动（模拟崩溃率0.176 vs 随机参数0.008），并通过反事实分析发现杠杆效应是主要放大因素。对量化风控系统和闪崩预警策略开发具有实用价值。

title: Predicting Factor Decay: ML Models for Cross-Factor Predictability Erosion
summary: We develop ML models that predict when cross-factor predictability will erode, enabling prospective risk management. A decay prediction model achieves C-index $= 0.93$ on held-out factor pairs, providing early warning of signal erosion---the key predictor is initial signal strength: stronger signals decay faster (``regression to the mean''). An online regime detector enables real-time classification with 6.6-day average detection delay. Prior work explains why factors decay (arbitrage, publication effects); we predict when decay will occur. Limitation: The primary HML$\to$SMB signal does not replicate in post-break OOS (2013--2024); this null result is consistent with genuine decay but limits confirmatory claims. Motivation: Among 30 directed Fama-French factor pairs (1990--2024), predictability targeting the Size factor (SMB) decays fastest. Of 7 pairs showing exponential decay ($R^2 > 0.3$), 4 target SMB (Mkt-RF$\to$SMB, CMA$\to$SMB, HML$\to$SMB, RMW$\to$SMB; half-lives 2.4--4.1 years). This SMB-concentration pattern motivates the predictive models. Methodology: Using a regime-conditional Granger framework with Student-$t$ HMMs, we document structural breaks clustering around June 1998 ($p < 10^{-10}$). A pre-break OOS test (HMM trained 1990--1995, tested 1996--2007) confirms signals existed: HML$\to$SMB shows $p = 0.013$ (Elevated) and $p < 0.001$ (Crisis). The primary HML$\to$SMB signal does not replicate in post-break OOS (2013--2024), consistent with genuine decay rather than overfitting---after ${\sim}6$ half-lives, the expected signal is $<$1% of its 1990s peak. International analysis finds 2/4 non-US markets with Bonferroni-surviving OOS effects; correction for full specification search was not applied, so results remain exploratory.
core_methodology: The paper employs a regime-conditional Granger framework with Student-t Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to predict the erosion of cross-factor predictability. It also uses machine learning models for decay prediction and online regime detection to classify real-time factor decay.
data_sources: The study uses Fama-French factor pairs from 1990 to 2024, focusing on directed factor pairs, particularly those targeting the Size factor (SMB). International market data is also analyzed for non-US markets.
alpha_potential: The research identifies and predicts when factor predictability will erode, which is crucial for dynamic factor timing and risk management. The key insight is that stronger signals decay faster, providing a potential edge in adjusting factor exposures before decay occurs.
title_cn: 预测因子衰减：用于跨因子预测性侵蚀的机器学习模型
summary_cn: 本研究开发了机器学习模型，用于预测跨因子预测性何时会衰减，从而实现前瞻性风险管理。通过使用基于Granger框架和隐马尔可夫模型的方法，研究发现初始信号强度是衰减的关键预测指标。该模型在实时分类中表现出色，平均检测延迟为6.6天，适用于动态因子调整和风险控制。

title: Nonparametric GARCH: An Iterated Neural Estimator
summary: We study nonparametric estimation and forecasting for GARCH-type processes and propose an iterated neural estimator that alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating the unobserved conditional variances. Under mild conditions, we establish finite-sample bounds for the time-averaged in-sample variance-path error and show that the estimator is minimax rate-optimal up to logarithmic factors. Under stationarity and mixing conditions, we establish the same rate for recursion-map estimation and derive finite-sample bounds for out-of-sample variance forecasts and expected excess Gaussian quasi-likelihood (QLIKE) loss. The convergence rates depend on the true lag orders and remain unchanged when the fitted orders are overspecified. Simulation studies illustrate the effectiveness of our estimators under nonlinear and time-varying volatility dynamics. Real-data applications suggest that our neural methods perform competitively and can incorporate option-price and high-frequency information.
core_methodology: The paper proposes an iterated neural estimator for nonparametric GARCH-type processes, which alternates between estimating the recursion map and updating the unobserved conditional variances. The method is shown to be minimax rate-optimal under certain conditions and performs well in both in-sample and out-of-sample forecasting.
data_sources: The paper mentions real-data applications that can incorporate option-price and high-frequency information, suggesting the use of both traditional market data and alternative data sources.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to handle nonlinear and time-varying volatility dynamics could provide an edge in volatility forecasting and risk management, which are crucial for quantitative trading strategies. The incorporation of option-price and high-frequency data further enhances its potential for generating alpha.
title_cn: 非参数GARCH：一种迭代神经估计器
summary_cn: 本文研究非参数GARCH类过程的估计与预测，提出一种迭代神经估计器，交替估计递归映射和更新未观测条件方差。该方法在非线性与时变波动动态下表现优异，可结合期权价格与高频数据，为量化交易中的波动率预测与风险管理提供新工具。

title: Estimating "Realized" Skewness using Convolutional Neural Network
summary: We propose a new estimator of low-frequency skewness (monthly) that exploits high-frequency data (5 min) through a direct functional mapping consisting of layers of Convolutional Neural Networks followed by Multi Layer Perceptrons. Monte Carlo experiments involving stochastic volatility models, with and without jumps, show that the estimator reduces finite-sample bias relative to existing realized-skewness estimators and remains accurate under model misspecification. Empirically, our estimator exhibits temporal stability and delivers cross-sectional performance in actual skewness-sorted portfolios. We characterize the finite-sample bias of conventional plug-in skewness estimators and establish risk consistency properties of the proposed NN estimator under standard regularity conditions.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a new estimator for low-frequency skewness using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) followed by Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs). This approach directly maps high-frequency (5-minute) data to monthly skewness estimates, addressing finite-sample bias and maintaining accuracy under model misspecification.
data_sources: High-frequency market data (5-minute intervals) is used to estimate monthly skewness. The method is validated through Monte Carlo experiments with stochastic volatility models, both with and without jumps.
alpha_potential: The estimator demonstrates temporal stability and performs well in cross-sectional skewness-sorted portfolios, suggesting potential for improved risk assessment and portfolio optimization. The reduction in finite-sample bias could enhance strategies reliant on accurate skewness estimation, such as volatility trading or skewness-based factor investing.
title_cn: 使用卷积神经网络估计'已实现'偏度
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种新的低频偏度估计方法，利用卷积神经网络和多层感知器直接映射高频数据（5分钟）到月度偏度估计。蒙特卡洛实验表明，该估计器减少了有限样本偏差，并在模型错误设定下保持准确性。实证结果显示，该估计器具有时间稳定性，并在实际偏度排序组合中表现出色，可用于改进风险管理和组合优化策略。

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
summary: We introduce TabPFN-3.5, our new flagship Tabular Foundation Model. It significantly outperforms its predecessor, TabPFN-3, and all existing baselines across a broad range of tabular problems. TabPFN-3.5 sets a new state of the art on standard tabular prediction in TabArena, and extends it to the data practitioners encounter in practice: non-i.i.d. data with temporal or grouped splits, tables with strings, text and images, high-cardinality categorical features, and wide tables with many features. These gains carry over to our task-specific harnesses: state of the art on relational data and stronger time-series forecasting. For faster inference, our variant TabPFN-3.5-Fast runs up to 3x faster than TabPFN-3 while keeping most of the accuracy gains. In addition, we upgrade TabPFN-3.5-Plus, expanding our multimodal capabilities with advanced text and date handling alongside proprietary inference optimizations. Finally, we release a new version of our Thinking mode, TabPFN-3.5-Thinking, which scales inference-time computation to push the state of the art further. It benefits from our stronger base model and from inference-time improvements that make it up to 12x faster than TabPFN-3-Thinking.
core_methodology: TabPFN-3.5 is a tabular foundation model that excels in handling various tabular data challenges, including non-i.i.d. data, high-cardinality categorical features, and multimodal data (text, images). It introduces task-specific harnesses for relational data and time-series forecasting, along with optimized variants for faster inference and enhanced capabilities.
data_sources: The model is designed for general tabular data, which can include financial time-series data, relational datasets (e.g., stock fundamentals), and multimodal data (e.g., earnings reports with text and images).
alpha_potential: The model's strength in handling complex tabular data and time-series forecasting suggests potential for generating alpha in factor investing, stock selection, and macroeconomic forecasting. Its ability to process multimodal data (e.g., text in earnings reports) could also uncover inefficiencies in sentiment-driven markets.
title_cn: TabPFN-3.5：技术报告
summary_cn: TabPFN-3.5是一种先进的表格基础模型，在非独立同分布数据、高基数分类特征和多模态数据处理方面表现卓越。该模型在时间序列预测和关系数据处理上的优势，使其在量化交易中具有潜在应用价值，特别是在因子投资、股票选择和宏观经济预测领域。其快速推理版本（TabPFN-3.5-Fast）和增强的多模态处理能力（TabPFN-3.5-Plus）进一步提升了实际交易场景中的实用性。

title: TStruct: Learning Shared Temporal Structures for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
summary: Long-term time series forecasting requires learning temporal dependencies that remain stable and generalizable under temporal distribution shifts. However, real-world time series are often noisy, non-stationary, and heterogeneous, making deep learning models prone to overfitting incidental temporal interactions in the training data. This raises a question: when observations are difficult to align, could temporal relationships be easier to reuse? To investigate this possibility, we analyze patch-level temporal relationship matrices across commonly used time series datasets, revealing dominant patterns shared across different temporal windows and variables. Comparisons with patch-shuffled and IID Gaussian controls further support the presence of reusable temporal relationship structures. Motivated by these findings, we propose \textbf{T}emporal \textbf{Struct}ure Network (\textbf{TStruct}), a simple yet effective network that learns reusable temporal dependency structures and adaptively combines them for each sample and variable. Specifically, TStruct directly parameterizes a set of shared temporal dependency matrices and generates normalized combination weights using dynamic sample information and static variable priors. These weights represent a soft allocation of each sample-variable pair over shared temporal dependency structures, enabling the model to generate adaptive temporal dependency matrices under shared structural constraints, rather than fitting incidental interactions in a fully unconstrained manner. Notably, TStruct consistently outperforms several strong baselines across all evaluated datasets, achieving superior accuracy while maintaining high computational efficiency. Our code is available at https://github.com/yangzeli/TStruct.
core_methodology: TStruct learns shared temporal dependency structures across different time series and adaptively combines them for each sample and variable, using parameterized temporal dependency matrices and dynamic combination weights.
data_sources: Commonly used time series datasets (specific datasets not named in abstract, but methodology is generalizable to financial time series)
alpha_potential: The method's ability to identify and leverage reusable temporal structures could help capture persistent market patterns that survive distribution shifts, potentially uncovering stable predictive signals in noisy financial data.
title_cn: TStruct：用于长期时间序列预测的共享时间结构学习
summary_cn: TStruct通过学习和共享时间依赖结构，自适应地组合这些结构进行预测，在存在时间分布偏移时仍保持稳健性。该方法可应用于金融时间序列预测，识别市场中的持久性模式，为量化交易提供稳定的预测信号。

title: Latent Cluster Separation as a Regularizer for Lifelong Anomaly Detection
summary: Lifelong (continual) anomaly detection systems must learn a sequence of tasks without forgetting how to recognize anomaly types seen earlier -- a property known as backward transfer. A common way to try to improve backward transfer is to reshape a model's internal representation around learnable concept centroids, typically coupled with a new way of scoring anomalies based on distance to those centroids. Because these two design choices are usually introduced together, it is unclear which one is actually responsible for any performance gain. In this paper, we unbundle the two mechanisms within a VAE-based lifelong anomaly detector and study them separately. We find that used purely as a training-time regularizer -- while leaving anomaly scoring unchanged -- latent cluster separation can improve detection quality and backward transfer, though whether it outperforms the alternative scoring approach depends on the dataset's underlying representation. Switching to distance-based scoring is instead where most of the instability commonly associated with this class of method actually originates; we identify and explain the underlying mechanism. This benefit depends on the dataset's underlying representation, and we report this as practical guidance for choosing between the two design choices, rather than as a list of caveats.
core_methodology: The paper explores latent cluster separation as a training-time regularizer within a VAE-based framework for lifelong anomaly detection, comparing its effects with distance-based scoring methods.
data_sources: The methodology is general and could be applied to various types of financial time series or market microstructure data where anomaly detection is relevant, though specific data sources are not mentioned in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The approach could potentially identify anomalous market behaviors or structural breaks in financial time series, which could be valuable for risk management or detecting early signals of market regime changes.
title_cn: 潜在聚类分离作为终身异常检测的正则化方法
summary_cn: 本研究探索了在VAE框架下使用潜在聚类分离作为训练时正则化方法，以提高终身异常检测的稳定性和性能。对于金融应用，该方法可能帮助持续识别市场异常行为和结构变化，适用于风险管理或市场状态监测系统。主要价值在于其持续学习能力而不遗忘早期异常模式的特征识别能力。

title: Stress-Testing the Robustness of LLM-Based Causal Inference
summary: Why do some of the world's most powerful Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems still struggle to reason about cause and effect? Causal discovery, the ability to discern the underlying drivers of a system, is fundamental to scientific inquiry and has traditionally relied on structured data and statistical methods. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been explored as an alternative paradigm for causal inference, leveraging their broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. Yet, despite their linguistic fluency, LLMs often rely on surface-level pattern recognition rather than genuine causal logic. While it is known that LLMs stumble in this domain, we lack a precise map of where, why, and how significantly these failures occur. In this paper, we propose a systematic stress-test framework across six critical dimensions: model scale, causal graph complexity, prompting strategy, metadata quality, data quality, and sensitivity to uncertainty. Our findings reveal a significant "optimism bias" in LLMs; models consistently overestimate causal links, leading to low precision across the board. Furthermore, we demonstrate that traditional evaluation metrics can be deceptive: while reasoning-heavy models lead in performance, the highest scores often occur when uncertainty in inference is overlooked. Once uncertainty is integrated into the evaluation, performance drops, providing a more honest reflection of causal reliability. We also find that, while scaling model size improves outcomes, these gains are fragile; performance degrades sharply as the quality of metadata decreases. This work serves as a practical guide to the blind spots of LLMs, offering a clear-eyed assessment of when these tools can be integrated into a causal discovery pipeline and when they are likely to lead researchers astray.
core_methodology: Systematic stress-test framework for evaluating LLMs' causal inference capabilities across six dimensions: model scale, causal graph complexity, prompting strategy, metadata quality, data quality, and sensitivity to uncertainty.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely involves synthetic or real-world datasets with known causal structures for testing LLMs.
alpha_potential: The paper's findings on LLMs' limitations in causal inference could inform the development of more robust AI models for financial prediction tasks, particularly in identifying true causal relationships in market data. However, direct alpha generation would require significant adaptation to financial datasets.
title_cn: 基于大语言模型的因果推断鲁棒性压力测试
summary_cn: 本研究通过系统压力测试框架评估了大语言模型(LLM)在因果推断中的表现，发现模型存在过度乐观偏差和低精确度问题。这些发现对金融领域应用LLM进行市场因果关系分析具有重要警示意义，提示需谨慎评估模型输出的因果可靠性，特别是在处理复杂金融数据时需结合不确定性量化。

title: Enhancing Stock Market Information Retrieval with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Natural Language Processing (NLP) has been widely applied in financial domains, enabling automated analysis and retrieval of stock market information. However, traditional NLP-based systems often struggle with maintaining contextual accuracy and generating relevant responses in dynamic financial environments. To address these challenges, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models have emerged as a powerful solution, combining retrieval-based methods with generative capabilities to enhance response quality. In this study, we present a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system designed to generate responses related to stock market information. The system integrates retrieval-based and generative approaches to enhance the accuracy and relevance of financial text generation. To evaluate its effectiveness, we employ the ROUGE metric, specifically ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L, to measure lexical and structural similarity between generated and reference texts. Experimental results on a dataset of 100 stock market-related queries demonstrate high ROUGE scores, indicating strong alignment with reference documents. Additionally, we assess latency to evaluate the system responsiveness, achieving an average response time of 1.16 seconds. These findings confirm that our RAG model is capable of providing accurate and timely stock market insights, making it a promising approach for financial information retrieval.
core_methodology: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combining retrieval-based methods with generative capabilities to enhance the accuracy and relevance of financial text generation.
data_sources: Dataset of 100 stock market-related queries and reference documents.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve information retrieval and generation for trading decisions by providing more accurate and timely stock market insights, though direct alpha generation is not demonstrated.
title_cn: 利用检索增强生成技术提升股市信息检索能力
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于检索增强生成（RAG）的系统，用于生成与股市信息相关的响应。该系统结合了检索和生成方法，提高了金融文本生成的准确性和相关性。实验结果表明，该系统在100个股市相关查询的数据集上取得了较高的ROUGE分数，平均响应时间为1.16秒。这一方法为金融信息检索提供了准确和及时的见解，具有潜在的交易应用价值。

title: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging for Efficient Long-to-Short Reasoning
summary: Long-to-Short (L2S) model merging seeks to combine the strong reasoning capability of long chain-of-thought models with the concise style of base models, but existing methods that rely on linear interpolation and first-order activation statistics fail to capture how the loss landscape responds to parameter displacement, leading to degraded accuracy on hard tasks. We propose Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging (LHM), a training-free framework that replaces heuristic statistics with lightweight second-order curvature information. LHM consists of three components: (1) a low-rank Hessian approximation that efficiently estimates per-layer Hessian traces via Hutchinson's estimator on random inputs, eliminating the need for task-specific data; (2) a Layer Second-Order Sensitivity (LSOS) index that combines Hessian trace with task-vector norm to quantify per-layer fusion difficulty; and (3) a Dual-Constraint Coefficient Mapping (DCCM) that converts LSOS scores into layer-adaptive merge coefficients while jointly satisfying a fusion-error bound and a global length-reduction target. Experiments across six mathematical benchmarks on 1.5B and 7B models show that LHM outperforms state-of-the-art methods such as ACM-TIES and ORCA, achieving over 4\% accuracy gain and up to 93.1\% reduction in output length relative to the long-CoT model.
core_methodology: Low-Rank Hierarchical Merging (LHM) is a training-free framework that uses lightweight second-order curvature information to merge long chain-of-thought models with base models. It includes a low-rank Hessian approximation, a Layer Second-Order Sensitivity (LSOS) index, and a Dual-Constraint Coefficient Mapping (DCCM) to optimize model merging.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on mathematical benchmarks for evaluation.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to improve the efficiency and accuracy of financial models that require long reasoning chains, such as those used in algorithmic trading or risk assessment, by merging complex models with simpler ones without significant loss in performance.
title_cn: 低秩层次合并实现高效长到短推理
summary_cn: 本文提出的低秩层次合并（LHM）框架通过轻量级二阶曲率信息，高效合并长链思维模型与基础模型，可潜在提升金融领域复杂模型（如算法交易或风险评估）的效率与准确性，而无需显著性能损失。

title: ExaTune: Exhaustive Hyperparameter Landscape Exploration at Scale
summary: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) returns a single optimal configuration, systematically discarding the explored performance landscape that encodes how results depend on configuration choices. Fitness landscape analysis comprises a robust collection of methods from evolutionary computation offering ruggedness indices, autocorrelation functions, and fitness-distance correlation that have never been applied to machine learning hyperparameter spaces at scale, given that fine-grained ground-truth enumeration data has not existed. We present ExaTune, an open-source HPC system to produce a new artifact class: the hyperparameter landscape map. ExaTune exhaustively evaluates every point on a discretized hyperparameter grid via $K$-fold cross-validation, aggregates results into reproducible parquet benchmarks, and applies a suite of five formalized landscape metrics: spatial autocorrelation (Moran's $I$), ruggedness, local optima density, fitness-distance correlation (FDC), and variance-based parameter importance. We release a benchmark collection of 8 complete landscape maps (totalling 285,080 exhaustively evaluated configurations) spanning five model families (SVMs, random forests, XGBoost, ridge regression, and $k$-nearest neighbors) across six classification and two regression benchmarks, hosted on HuggingFace. Empirical analysis demonstrates that Bayesian optimization, Optuna, Hyperband, and Random Search at standard trial budgets systematically miss instability regions, secondary optima, and parameter interaction effects that are visible in complete landscapes; information that is structurally unavailable to any optimizer by design.
core_methodology: Exhaustive hyperparameter optimization with landscape analysis using spatial autocorrelation, ruggedness, local optima density, fitness-distance correlation, and variance-based parameter importance
data_sources: Benchmark datasets for classification and regression tasks (not financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve ML model performance in trading strategies by better understanding hyperparameter landscapes, though not directly applicable to market data
title_cn: ExaTune：大规模超参数空间的全面探索
summary_cn: ExaTune通过系统性地探索和量化超参数空间中的性能变化，为机器学习模型调优提供了新方法。虽然研究未直接使用金融数据，但其揭示的超参数相互作用和局部最优区域识别技术，可潜在提升量化交易中预测模型的稳定性和表现。

title: The Information Limits of Neural Controlled Differential Equations Under Sparse Observations
summary: Neural controlled differential equations (Neural CDEs) evolve hidden states along continuous paths constructed by interpolating discrete observations. Sparse measurements leave the input between observation times undetermined, and admissible continuous paths consistent with the same data can produce different terminal states. We characterize this ambiguity for planar drivers with bounded speed. The set of compatible terminal states admits a leading-order zonotopic approximation determined by feasible signed areas and transported Lie brackets. Its projection onto a scalar prediction yields a computable, target-specific ambiguity certificate. We also study the number of measurements needed to reduce the remaining uncertainty. For nondegenerate planar CDEs, the optimal worst-case radius over deterministic adaptive sampling policies scales as $N^{-1}$ when speed is bounded and $N^{-2}$ when both speed and acceleration are bounded, where $N$ is the number of observation intervals. Synthetic experiments assess the certificate using admissible continuous completions and examine the role of path regularity.
core_methodology: Neural Controlled Differential Equations (Neural CDEs) for modeling continuous-time dynamics from sparse observations, with analysis of uncertainty bounds and sampling requirements
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any time-series financial data (e.g., tick data, OHLC bars) where observations may be sparse
alpha_potential: Potential for improving continuous-time modeling of financial instruments where sparse observations create uncertainty (e.g., illiquid assets, overnight gaps). The ambiguity certificates could help quantify model risk in trading strategies.
title_cn: 稀疏观测下神经控制微分方程的信息极限
summary_cn: 该研究分析了神经控制微分方程在稀疏金融数据下的信息极限，提出了终端状态不确定性的量化方法。对于量化交易，该框架可改进对流动性不足资产或隔夜跳空的连续时间建模，其开发的模糊性证书有助于评估交易策略中的模型风险。

title: Decision Transformer with Task-Aware Representations for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning
summary: To enable effective generalization in offline meta-RL, it is essential to accurately infer the underlying task through latent task representations, which provide a compact and transferable summary of task-specific characteristics for guiding policy generation. In this paper, we propose Contrastive Task-Aware Decision Transformer (CoTA-DT), a DT-based offline meta-RL framework that learns task representations by jointly integrating four complementary components: (i) contrastive learning from offline trajectories, (ii) alignment with natural-language task descriptions, (iii) one-step supervision via a task-conditioned world model, and (iv) long-term supervision via a task-conditioned Q function. The learned task representations are used as conditioning signals for a DT-based policy, enabling task-aware meta-policy learning. To further support generalization in both zero-shot and few-shot settings, we design a language-grounded, self-adaptive strategy that enables effective and reliable adaptation to unseen tasks. Notably, in CoTA-DT, the pretrained LLM serves as a shared backbone for language encoding, world modeling, Q-function estimation, and policy learning. This unified design facilitates parameter sharing, improving both efficiency and generalization. Extensive experiments across diverse offline meta-RL benchmarks demonstrate that CoTA-DT consistently outperforms prior methods, particularly in challenging zero-shot generalization scenarios.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Contrastive Task-Aware Decision Transformer (CoTA-DT), which combines contrastive learning, natural-language task descriptions, task-conditioned world modeling, and Q-function estimation to learn task representations for offline meta-reinforcement learning. These representations are then used to condition a Decision Transformer (DT)-based policy for task-aware meta-policy learning.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on offline trajectories and natural-language task descriptions, which could be adapted to financial time-series data or alternative data like news and reports.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to identify and exploit market regimes or tasks (e.g., bull/bear markets, volatility regimes) by learning task representations from historical data. The integration of natural-language descriptions could also enable the use of financial news or reports to enhance task inference and policy adaptation.
title_cn: 基于任务感知表征的决策变换器在离线元强化学习中的应用
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种结合对比学习和自然语言任务描述的决策变换器框架（CoTA-DT），用于离线元强化学习。该方法通过学习任务表征来指导策略生成，可潜在应用于金融市场中的多任务学习，如识别不同市场状态并自适应调整交易策略。

title: Language Model Augmented Decision Transformer for Multi-Task Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: Offline multi-task reinforcement learning (MTRL) aims to learn a unified policy from heterogeneous offline datasets that generalizes across tasks. However, existing offline MTRL methods often struggle with two fundamental issues: severe per-task data scarcity and limited cross-task generalization. In this paper, we propose Language-Model Augmented Decision Transformer (LaMA-DT), a unified sequence-modeling framework that leverages a single large language model (LLM) for both trajectory augmentation and multi-task policy learning. LaMA-DT uses natural-language task descriptions to guide task-aligned trajectory augmentation through a set of supervised generation and alignment objectives, and incorporates a scoring-and-filtering mechanism to retain high-quality augmented trajectories. The same LLM is then repurposed as a language-conditioned Decision Transformer and fine-tuned on a mixture of real and augmented data. Experiments on Meta-World and MuJoCo multi-task benchmarks demonstrate that LaMA-DT consistently outperforms competitive baselines, particularly in low-data regimes, showing that language-guided data augmentation substantially improves cross-task generalization.
core_methodology: Uses a large language model (LLM) for both trajectory augmentation and multi-task policy learning in offline reinforcement learning, with natural-language task descriptions guiding the augmentation process.
data_sources: Meta-World and MuJoCo multi-task benchmarks (simulated environments), but methodology could be adapted to financial time-series data.
alpha_potential: Potential for cross-task generalization in trading strategies, especially in low-data regimes or for multi-strategy systems. Language-guided augmentation could help with rare market regimes.
title_cn: 语言模型增强的决策Transformer在多任务离线强化学习中的应用
summary_cn: 该研究提出LaMA-DT框架，利用大语言模型进行轨迹增强和多任务策略学习。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于低数据环境下的多策略系统，通过语言引导的数据增强改善跨市场状态的泛化能力，尤其适用于罕见市场行情的策略适应。

title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
summary: Foundation models in changing environments can encounter unfamiliar domain knowledge that their original training did not cover. However, new domains rarely provide large amounts of expert-created training data or reliable supervisory signals for further training. We introduce Recursa, a foundation model system that adapts to new domains by learning from its own experience without human experts or a stronger teacher model. Recursa uses a knowledge repository to store what it learns: domain-specific skills and instructions on when to apply them, along with memories of past task experiences and reflections on what to improve. Recursa bootstraps the repository from domain materials and then refines it through recursive self-improvement. It uses parallel learners to execute tasks and synthesize local improvements, then validates and merges the improvements into the knowledge repository. On Harvey LAB's Firm Knowledge benchmark, Recursa raises the all-pass rate on held-out test tasks from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash.
core_methodology: Recursive self-improvement system for foundation models using a knowledge repository to store and refine domain-specific skills and memories without human supervision.
data_sources: Unspecified in abstract, but implied to be domain materials and past task experiences in new domains.
alpha_potential: Potential to adapt quickly to new market regimes or financial domains where traditional models fail due to lack of training data, possibly uncovering new signals in emerging markets or instruments.
title_cn: Recursa：向递归自我改进的基础模型系统
summary_cn: Recursa采用递归自我改进机制，通过知识库存储和优化领域特定技能，无需人工监督即可适应新领域。在金融领域，可快速适应市场变化或新兴工具，潜在生成传统模型无法捕捉的信号。

title: Graph-Localized Coverage for Conformal Prediction on Inductive Graphs
summary: Conformal prediction (CP) provides marginal coverage guarantees, but marginal coverage does not determine where prediction errors occur on a graph. Queries from different graph neighborhoods can exhibit substantially different levels of uncertainty even when aggregate coverage remains near its target. We introduce GLocalCP, an online CP framework for inductive node classification and edge prediction that combines marginal and graph-local calibration with uncertainty-adaptive prediction sets. Specifically, GLocalCP puts forth a novel uncertainty-adaptive nonconformality score that relies on the mutual information obtained from Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout based prediction. Then, it augments a global online threshold with a kernel-based local correction that propagates coverage feedback among similar graph queries. On the theoretical horizon, we establish pathwise $O(N^{-1/2})$ marginal calibration error without exchangeability or stationarity and, for the exact-kernel formulation, an explicit $O(N^{-1/2})$ graph-localized calibration guarantee. Experiments on seven node-classification and seven edge-prediction benchmarks show that similar marginal coverage can conceal substantially different local reliability. Our proposed GLocalCP maintains coverage near the target while consistently reducing graph-local calibration error. Uncertainty scaling in GLocalCP further reduces prediction-set size across all evaluated node and edge datasets while leaving marginal coverage essentially unchanged.
core_methodology: GLocalCP combines conformal prediction with graph-local calibration and uncertainty-adaptive prediction sets, using Monte-Carlo dropout for uncertainty estimation and kernel-based local correction for coverage feedback propagation.
data_sources: Node-classification and edge-prediction benchmarks (not explicitly financial datasets but methodology is transferable to financial graph data like transaction networks or asset correlation graphs).
alpha_potential: Potential for improving reliability of graph-based trading signals (e.g., in cross-asset correlation trading or fraud detection) by providing localized uncertainty estimates and adaptive prediction sets that maintain coverage guarantees across different market regimes.
title_cn: 归纳图上的共形预测的图局部覆盖方法
summary_cn: GLocalCP框架通过结合边际校准和图局部校准，为金融图数据（如资产关联网络）提供具有局部不确定性适应的预测集。该方法可提升交易信号可靠性，特别适用于不同市场环境下需要动态调整预测置信度的场景，如跨资产套利或风险传染分析。

title: AlgoPilot: Cross-Paradigm Reasoning in Language Models via Strategy Selection and Guidance
summary: Real-world problems span diverse domains, including program synthesis, symbolic reasoning, planning, and optimization, and often require fundamentally different solution paradigms. A central challenge for LLM-based reasoning is twofold: identifying an appropriate problem-solving approach and formulating it correctly. In this paper, we propose AlgoPilot, a cross-paradigm reasoning framework that enables adaptive selection of the solving approaches and structured problem formulation prior to execution. The AlgoPilot framework contains three components: 1) a SteerLM, trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), that adaptively selects the solving strategy (paradigm and modes) based on input problems, 2) the corresponding expert GuideLM, trained via SFT, that generates structured formulation guidance tailored to the selected strategy, and 3) an ExecutionLM that generates solutions conditioned on both the selected strategy and its formulation. Unlike prompting-based methods that rely on fixed reasoning templates, our approach learns to adaptively choose and structure problem-solving strategies based on the input. We build AlgoPilot on Qwen3-8B and evaluate across 5 problem categories and 13 benchmarks with 66 unique domains, comparing against both the latest similarly scaled small models and large LLMs. AlgoPilot significantly improves average accuracy for the same model from 38.4% to 72.9%, outperforming the best large LLM prompting baseline GLM-5 by 11.7%. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each component. Notably, we show that the learned steering and formulation modules can transfer across execution models, suggesting their potential to improve other LLMs. Project page: https://sites.google.com/view/algopilot.
core_methodology: AlgoPilot is a cross-paradigm reasoning framework that adaptively selects problem-solving strategies (paradigms and modes) and generates structured formulation guidance before execution. It consists of three components: SteerLM for strategy selection, GuideLM for structured guidance generation, and ExecutionLM for solution generation.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but demonstrates the framework's effectiveness across 5 problem categories and 13 benchmarks with 66 unique domains, suggesting potential adaptability to financial datasets.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to adaptively select and structure problem-solving strategies could be leveraged for developing dynamic trading strategies that adjust to changing market conditions, potentially uncovering alpha through improved decision-making processes.
title_cn: AlgoPilot：通过策略选择与引导实现语言模型的跨范式推理
summary_cn: AlgoPilot是一种跨范式推理框架，通过自适应选择解决策略并生成结构化指导，可应用于量化交易中的动态策略调整。其核心在于结合强化学习与监督微调，优化决策流程，有望提升交易系统的适应性与表现。

title: The Evolution Strategies Paradox: Better Models from Worse Perturbations
summary: How is it possible for perturbation-based methods like Evolution Strategies (ES) to optimize billion-parameter large language models (LLMs)? Classical search methods are highly dependent on finding good candidates within generated populations. However, when using ES to fine-tune LLMs, a phenomenon can occur where all offspring models consistently perform worse than the parent model, yet during training, the parent model consistently improves. This paradox occurs across models, tasks, and even modalities. This paper characterizes the paradox, then examines how the local reward landscape and properties of the ES estimator contribute to it: in high-dimensional spaces, exploration leads to worse performance, yet still highlights good directions; aggregating those directions then allows for making local improvements. The result can be seen as a new optimization paradigm where a principled interaction of noise and curvature produces the paradox as a byproduct of effective optimization. These findings provide guidance for taking advantage of perturbation-based methods in LLM fine-tuning and in high-dimensional optimization in general.
core_methodology: The paper explores the paradox in Evolution Strategies (ES) where worse-performing perturbations can still lead to better model optimization, especially in high-dimensional spaces like LLM fine-tuning. It analyzes the local reward landscape and the properties of the ES estimator to explain this phenomenon.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on general high-dimensional optimization problems, which could theoretically include financial time series or market data.
alpha_potential: The findings could be adapted to optimize trading strategies in high-dimensional spaces, such as multi-factor models or complex portfolio optimizations, by leveraging the paradox where noisy perturbations still provide useful gradient directions.
title_cn: 进化策略悖论：从更差的扰动中得到更好的模型
summary_cn: 本文研究了进化策略（ES）中的悖论现象：在高维空间中，较差的扰动仍能为模型优化提供有效方向。这一发现可应用于量化交易中的高维策略优化（如多因子模型或组合优化），通过利用噪声扰动提取有效梯度信息，提升策略表现。

title: RGDM: Robust Graph Diffusion Model
summary: Diffusion models represent a powerful class of generative models known for their solid theoretical foundations and remarkable performance across diverse tasks and domains. Existing node level diffusion methods synthesize nodes and edges within a graph, but are not designed to learn a robust generator from adversarially corrupted graphs. In this study, we introduce the Robust Graph Diffusion Model (RGDM), designed to generate labeled synthetic graph structures consisting of nodes and edges that integrate seamlessly into a given graph. The RGDM consists of a Robust Graph Autoencoder (RGAE) and a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM). Leveraging an edge selection mechanism and an innovative low-rank regularization on the latent feature, the RGDM produces clean and high-quality synthetic graph structures, even when trained on graphs subject to adversarial attacks. Comprehensive experimental evaluations reveal that Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) trained on the augmented graph, which is formed by merging the original attacked graph with the synthetic graph structures, exhibit significantly improved robustness against various graph adversarial attacks in the context of semi-supervised node classification. The code of the RGDM is available at https://github.com/Statistical-Deep-Learning/RGDM.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Robust Graph Diffusion Model (RGDM), which combines a Robust Graph Autoencoder (RGAE) and a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM) to generate synthetic graph structures that enhance the robustness of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) against adversarial attacks. The method includes an edge selection mechanism and low-rank regularization on latent features.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial datasets but focuses on graph-structured data, which could be adapted for financial networks (e.g., stock correlation graphs, transaction networks).
alpha_potential: The method could be adapted to improve the robustness of GNN-based trading strategies against adversarial noise or data corruption in financial graphs, potentially enhancing model reliability in noisy market conditions.
title_cn: 鲁棒图扩散模型（RGDM）
summary_cn: 该研究提出的鲁棒图扩散模型（RGDM）通过结合鲁棒图自编码器和潜在扩散模型，能够在对抗性攻击下生成高质量的合成图结构。该方法可增强图神经网络在半监督节点分类任务中的鲁棒性，为金融市场中基于图结构的交易策略（如股票关联网络分析）提供了抗噪声干扰的新思路。

title: On the Feature Evolution of Temporal Difference Learning
summary: Temporal-difference (TD) learning trains neural representations using bootstrapped targets generated by evolving value estimates, yet how predictive features emerge and propagate under incomplete neural updates remains poorly understood. We investigate this problem using finite-width two-layer ReLU critics on a constructed family of smooth stochastic horizon-$H$ MDPs with unknown quadratic structure and $d$-dimensional observations. We first show that an informative TD update acquires the quadratic Bellman signal and yields a representation admitting a bounded predictive readout.
