The simultaneous hidden-weight and head update achieves a strict finite-sample prediction-risk improvement over matched head-only SGD, with a $2(d+1)$-fold larger population quadratic response. We then establish that an imperfect learned continuation can already provide informative supervision to an earlier zero-reward stage. By tracking coupled neural updates with one SGD step per target copy, without requiring intermediate Bellman regressions to be solved, we obtain a uniform prediction-error transient $\exp[-\Omega(K/(Hd))]$, up to action-independent shifts and explicit sampling and finite-width errors. On the constructed signed-action MDP family whose total reward is bounded by 1, we show that an exploration-then-commit algorithm can achieve $\widetilde{O}(d^3H^{1/3}T^{2/3})$ regret over $T$ episodes, using $K=\widetilde{O}(Hd)$ global updates. Our analysis connects bootstrapped feature acquisition, concurrent neural refinement, and finite-budget policy performance.
core_methodology: Investigates temporal-difference (TD) learning with neural representations in stochastic MDPs, focusing on feature evolution and predictive performance under finite-width neural networks.
data_sources: Constructed family of smooth stochastic horizon-H MDPs with unknown quadratic structure and d-dimensional observations.
alpha_potential: Potential for improving predictive models in reinforcement learning-based trading strategies by better understanding feature evolution and TD learning dynamics.
title_cn: 论时序差分学习的特征演化
summary_cn: 本研究探讨了在有限宽度神经网络下时序差分学习中的特征演化问题，通过构建具有二次结构的随机MDP家族，展示了TD学习如何获取贝尔曼信号并改善预测性能。对于基于强化学习的量化交易策略开发具有理论指导价值。

title: A Parametric Linear Conic Projection for Structured Sparse Attention
summary: In this paper, we introduce the Cone Alignment Index (CAI), a scale-invariant sparsity measure associated with a Lorentz-cone geometry. We provide a probabilistic analysis of the distribution of the CAI score, including a general theorem and explicit corollaries for Gaussian and uniform distributions. As a consequence, we show that, in the high-sparsity regime, the probability that the samples lie within the convex cone tends to one. Building upon this formulation, we derive two complementary projections: the \emph{Parametric Linear Conic Projection} (PLCP), an efficient closed-form approximation, and the \emph{Parametric Euclidean Conic Projection} (PECP), the exact Euclidean projection onto the cone boundary. Our analysis establishes several fundamental theoretical properties. We prove that PLCP and PECP are collinear, differ only by a positive radial scaling factor, and induce exactly the same sparsity threshold, thereby preserving an identical active support. Furthermore, we derive a support-identification theorem showing that, for any prescribed sparsity level $l<n$, the number of coefficients discarded at each iteration is theoretically controlled. Building on this theoretical foundation, we develop a bilevel PLCP framework for structured matrix sparsification. The proposed method naturally generates hardware-friendly structured sparsity patterns, including row-wise, column-wise, and diagonal masks, making it particularly well suited for accelerating Transformer attention mechanisms.
core_methodology: Introduction of Cone Alignment Index (CAI) and Parametric Linear Conic Projection (PLCP) for structured sparsity in Transformer attention mechanisms.
data_sources: Abstract does not specify financial data sources, but methodology could be applied to financial time series for attention-based models.
alpha_potential: Potential to improve efficiency and performance of Transformer-based trading models through structured sparsity, possibly enhancing feature selection or reducing computational overhead.
title_cn: 结构化稀疏注意力的参数化线性锥投影
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于锥对齐指数（CAI）的结构化稀疏方法，包括参数化线性锥投影（PLCP）和参数化欧几里得锥投影（PECP），适用于优化Transformer注意力机制的结构化稀疏模式。在量化交易中，该方法可能提升基于注意力模型的金融时间序列分析效率，减少计算成本并改进特征选择。

title: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)
summary: LLM agents often give conflicting answers to the same question, and many deployed agents are variants of one base model, so their errors are correlated. We study truth discovery among such agents: inferring the true answer and each agent's reliability without labels. Classical truth-discovery and crowdsourcing estimators reward an agreeing bloc and can fall below majority vote. We propose BP-TD, which adds per-agent decorrelation weights to mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model, so that agents sharing a base model count together as about one vote. Its first iteration is exactly a weighted vote; later iterations estimate agent reliability. With 13 local agents on MMLU, BP-TD beats majority vote without any labels (0.716 vs. 0.624 on 160 questions; 0.707 vs. 0.674 on 10,000) and ranks agents by their true accuracy, which classical estimators invert. The gain depends on the pool: over 2,852 sub-pools of four benchmarks, decorrelation helps when the largest correlated bloc is weaker than the other agents and hurts when it is the strongest, and we found no label-free statistic that tells the two cases apart. Labels change the picture quickly: with 20 labelled questions, selecting the single best agent is more accurate than every aggregator we tested on MMLU, ARC and TruthfulQA.
core_methodology: BP-TD (Belief Propagation for Truth Discovery) is a method that uses per-agent decorrelation weights in mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model to estimate the true answer and agent reliability from conflicting responses of LLM agents.
data_sources: The paper uses responses from 13 local agents on the MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding) dataset, ARC, and TruthfulQA benchmarks.
alpha_potential: The method could be adapted to aggregate conflicting signals from multiple AI models in trading, potentially improving the reliability of AI-generated trading signals by decorrelating errors from models sharing a common base.
title_cn: 当AI代理意见不一致时，真相在哪里？基于依赖感知的信念传播的无监督真相发现（扩展版）
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种无监督方法BP-TD，通过解相关权重处理共享基础模型的LLM代理之间的冲突回答，在MMLU等基准测试中优于多数投票。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于聚合多个AI模型的交易信号，通过减少共享基础模型带来的相关性误差，提高信号可靠性。

title: AgenticFinBench: Benchmarking Financial Agents on Diverse Tasks from Real-World Requests
summary: Financial agents are becoming an important class of real-world AI systems. Financial tasks vary widely in type and difficulty, and many are open-ended with no ground-truth answers. However, existing benchmarks neither capture this breadth and open-endedness nor separate grounding from correctness. To bridge this gap, we introduce $\textbf{AgenticFinBench}$, a benchmark of 230 real-world financial tasks spanning 8 categories, 2 languages, and 4 complexity levels. We also propose a reference-free evaluation framework that combines question-specific rubrics with a two-stage claim audit that detects hallucinations, defined as claims absent from the agent's trace and refuted by external evidence. This framework better matches how financial work is assessed in practice. Experiments across 18 agent configurations reveal three key findings: (1) Ignoring hallucinations can overstate agent performance: hallucination auditing lowers the baseline leader's score by 7.58 points and moves it to fourth place. (2) Harness differences explain more variation in evidence grounding than model differences (28.6% vs 8.8%). (3) Quality scores fall from 89.44 on direct retrieval to 79.18 on the most complex tasks. Case studies show that agents struggle to explain how events affect company profits or stock prices, compare financial data on a consistent basis, and justify their conclusions. By releasing AgenticFinBench, we aim to advance financial reasoning, factual verification, and agent design for more reliable responses to diverse real-world financial requests. Our project page is at $\textbf{https://nashnovaresearch.github.io/AgenticFinBench/}$.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AgenticFinBench, a benchmark for evaluating financial agents across diverse real-world tasks, and proposes a reference-free evaluation framework that combines question-specific rubrics with a two-stage claim audit to detect hallucinations. This framework aims to better assess financial work by separating grounding from correctness.
data_sources: The benchmark includes 230 real-world financial tasks spanning 8 categories, 2 languages, and 4 complexity levels. The tasks are derived from real-world financial requests, though specific data sources are not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The benchmark and evaluation framework could help improve the reliability and accuracy of financial agents, which could be valuable for developing more robust AI-driven trading strategies. However, the direct alpha potential is limited as the focus is on benchmarking rather than generating trading signals.
title_cn: AgenticFinBench：基于真实世界请求的多样化任务对金融智能体进行基准测试
summary_cn: 该论文提出了AgenticFinBench，一个包含230个真实世界金融任务的基准测试，用于评估金融智能体在多样化任务中的表现。通过无参考评估框架和两阶段声明审计，该研究有助于提高金融智能体的可靠性和准确性，对开发更稳健的AI驱动交易策略具有潜在价值。

title: Amortized Nonlinear Variable Selection with Prior-Data Fitted Networks
summary: Variable selection is an important task for interpreting potentially complex systems in fields such as biology, business, and sociology. The importance of variable selection has attracted considerable attention in statistics and machine learning. In this paper, we are mainly interested in model-agnostic variable selection for identifying variables that have general nonlinear dependence on the response. We propose MambaPFN, short for Model-Agnostic Markov BlAnket selection with Prior-data Fitted Networks, which is built upon the Transformer, a building block of many popular large language models. Specifically, we consider a functional-mapping perspective on variable-selection learning, in which the Transformer is treated as a learnable mapping from a dataset to its relevant variables. To learn this mapping, MambaPFN introduces three new components: (i) a faithful, rich, and scalable scheme for generating pretraining data, (ii) an objective that targets each variable's posterior inclusion probability, and (iii) a modified Transformer architecture tailored to variable selection. Once pretrained, MambaPFN is applied to new datasets without parameter updates. Empirically, MambaPFN achieves desirable variable-selection performance in simulation studies and exhibits a scaling law---more pretraining datasets and larger models can continuously improve its performance. Applied to a Facebook comments dataset, MambaPFN selects the fewest variables and achieves the highest computational efficiency and predictive performance, improving upon the best baselines by about 20%.
core_methodology: The paper proposes MambaPFN, a model-agnostic variable selection method using a Transformer-based architecture to identify variables with nonlinear dependence on the response. It incorporates a pretraining scheme, a modified Transformer architecture, and an objective targeting posterior inclusion probabilities.
data_sources: The method is tested on a Facebook comments dataset, but its methodology can be generalized to financial datasets.
alpha_potential: The ability to select relevant variables with nonlinear dependence could be valuable for feature selection in quantitative trading models, potentially improving predictive performance by focusing on the most informative market variables.
title_cn: 基于先验数据拟合网络的摊销非线性变量选择
summary_cn: 本文提出MambaPFN方法，利用Transformer架构进行模型无关的变量选择，特别针对非线性依赖关系。该方法通过预训练和数据生成方案，可高效识别关键变量。在量化交易中，这种技术能优化特征选择流程，提升市场预测模型的准确性和计算效率。

title: Rethinking GA2Ms: performance and out-of-distribution generalisation
summary: Generalised Additive Models (GAMs) are a cornerstone of interpretable machine learning, offering transparent predictions through structured additive decompositions. Despite advances from classical GAMs to modern neural and spline-based variants, two notable gaps remain. First, comprehensive benchmarking of spline-based GAMs on large-scale tabular learning tasks, the dominant modality in applied settings, is lacking. Second, their robustness under distribution shift, a setting where structured inductive biases should confer advantages, remains unexplored. We propose a multi-resolution, higher-order Composite Generalised Additive Model (CoGA2M) and evaluate it on the TALENT benchmark suite. CoGA2M ranks in the top third across all baselines (29 for regression, 32 for classification), establishing competitive performance with state-of-the-art tabular methods. We further extend TALENT with out-of-distribution (OOD) splits exhibiting train-test distributional shift and benchmark CoGA2M against LightGBM, a consistently top-performing model on TALENT. Under distribution shift, CoGA2M outperforms LightGBM, demonstrating a clear structural advantage. Our results position spline-based GAMs as strong contenders for tabular prediction and reveal a previously unrecognised benefit of additive structure in the OOD regime.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a multi-resolution, higher-order Composite Generalised Additive Model (CoGA2M) for tabular data prediction, focusing on interpretability and robustness under distribution shift. It benchmarks against state-of-the-art tabular methods and evaluates performance on out-of-distribution data.
data_sources: The paper uses the TALENT benchmark suite, which includes large-scale tabular datasets for regression and classification tasks. Specific financial datasets are not mentioned, but the methodology is applicable to financial tabular data.
alpha_potential: The model's robustness under distribution shift and its interpretable structure could be valuable for financial applications where out-of-distribution generalization is critical, such as risk modeling and anomaly detection. However, direct alpha generation is not demonstrated.
title_cn: 重新思考GA2Ms：性能与分布外泛化
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种多分辨率高阶复合广义可加模型（CoGA2M），在TALENT基准测试中表现优异，尤其在分布偏移情况下优于LightGBM。其可解释性和鲁棒性在金融风险建模和异常检测中具有潜在应用价值。

title: When Self-Verification Hurts: Calibrated Answer Repair for Financial Question Answering
summary: Financial question answering can fail even when a model extracts a plausible number from the supplied evidence: the answer may attach it to the wrong entity, period, unit, or accounting concept. Asking the model to verify and revise its draft can help, but open-ended revision may alter content that was already correct or inspect the wrong relation and reinforce the original error. We formulate repair as a decision that balances the information it may recover against the correct content it may damage. Based on this trade-off, we introduce Calibrated Answer Repair (CAR), which first estimates whether a draft is likely to benefit from repair, then selects a targeted check, localizes the relevant evidence or draft span, and limits the permitted edit. Across FinRank, Fin-RATE, and FinQA with three open-weight models, CAR outperforms generic verification in all dataset-model settings. At the system level, it recovers 14.6% of initially missed answer requirements while damaging 2.1% of initially correct ones. Its post-draft token cost is over 30 percent lower than the iterative revision alternatives. Ablations on two dataset-model settings show that evidence localization and bounded editing are the main contributors to CAR's gains.
core_methodology: Calibrated Answer Repair (CAR) improves financial question answering by first estimating if a draft answer is likely to benefit from repair, then selects targeted checks, localizes relevant evidence or draft spans, and limits edits to prevent unnecessary changes. The methodology focuses on minimizing errors while maximizing correctness.
data_sources: Financial documents and datasets (FinRank, Fin-RATE, and FinQA) containing numerical and contextual financial information.
alpha_potential: The method could improve accuracy in extracting and interpreting financial data from documents, which is crucial for algorithmic trading and quantitative research. Better data accuracy reduces noise and improves signal extraction.
title_cn: 自我验证的弊端：校准答案修复在金融问答中的应用
summary_cn: 本研究提出的校准答案修复（CAR）方法通过精准定位和有限编辑，提升了金融问答的准确性。该方法可减少算法交易中数据提取错误，从而增强信号质量。

title: Provably Learning Mixtures of Linear Experts
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are widely deployed in modern machine learning. However, few convergence guarantees exist for gradient-based training of MoEs: the objective is nonconvex, and even simple mixtures trap first-order methods in spurious local optima. We analyze a canonical gated mixture featuring linear experts and a gate induced by Gaussian clusters in the input space, and give, to our knowledge, the first global convergence guarantee for jointly training the gate and the experts of such a model by gradient EM on its likelihood. Given a logarithmic overparameterization relative to the true number of experts $m$, gradient EM converges from randomly initialized gates and least-squares-initialized experts to any prescribed accuracy in polynomially many iterations, under a separation condition on the gate centers. Our analysis establishes a gradient-dominance inequality for the coupled dynamics by decoupling the loss into per-cluster subproblems. Empirical results validate the predicted $m\log m$ phase transition and suggest that the least-squares warm start required by our analysis is not needed in practice: randomly initialized experts perform nearly as well. We also find that leaving the mixing weights unconstrained concentrates routing onto the true number of experts, whereas load-balancing penalties spread it, so that the fitted model can be pruned to a fraction of its width without loss of accuracy.
core_methodology: The paper presents a global convergence guarantee for gradient EM training of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models with linear experts and Gaussian gate clusters. It demonstrates that with logarithmic overparameterization and proper initialization, the method can achieve any prescribed accuracy in polynomially many iterations under a separation condition on gate centers.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is general and could be applied to financial time series, market microstructure data, or other quantitative trading datasets.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to identify regime-switching behaviors in financial markets or to model different market conditions with specialized 'experts'. The theoretical guarantees provide confidence in the model's ability to learn meaningful patterns, which could be leveraged for trading signals.
title_cn: 可证明学习的线性专家混合模型
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种用于训练线性专家混合模型（MoE）的梯度EM算法的全局收敛保证，适用于金融市场中的状态切换建模。该方法通过过参数化和适当的初始化，可在多项式时间内达到任意精度，为量化交易中的多状态市场行为分析提供了理论支持。

title: Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift
summary: Distribution shifts, including covariate shifts, are ubiquitous in real-world applications of machine learning. Empirical evidence suggests that, across a variety of models with and without downstream adaptation, ensembles tend to be more robust to covariate shift than single models. We extend the theory of covariate shift severity from single models to ensembles, providing theoretical justification for the empirical trends. We introduce new discrepancy measures of covariate shift severity to control the risk of partition-based kernel estimators. We then show that with sufficient ensemble size, these models can achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift. Our results suggest that modelers can expect to need larger ensemble sizes for more severe covariate shifts.
core_methodology: The paper introduces new discrepancy measures for covariate shift severity and demonstrates that ensembles of random partition-based models can achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift. The methodology focuses on improving model robustness to distribution shifts through ensemble techniques.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is generally applicable to any dataset experiencing covariate shift, which could include financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The approach could be valuable for developing more robust trading models that maintain performance during market regime changes or other distribution shifts. The ensemble technique may help in creating more stable signals under varying market conditions.
title_cn: 协变量偏移下基于随机划分的模型集成
summary_cn: 该研究提出了新的协变量偏移严重性度量方法，并证明在足够大的集成规模下，基于随机划分的模型集成可以在协变量偏移下实现极小极大最优风险收敛率。对于量化交易，这种方法可提升模型在不同市场环境下的稳健性，特别是在处理市场机制变化时保持信号稳定性。

title: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models
summary: Implicit generative models based on deep neural networks have revolutionized many scientific fields, from weather research to language generation. They successfully model complex random objects arising in real-world problems. In this work, we propose a sample-efficient training mechanism for these models. Our approach leverages regularized inference with shrinkage priors and generalized Bayes. In the large $p$ (parameter dimension) and small $n$ (sample size) setting, sparsity-inducing priors have been successfully used for linear regression when $p \gg n$. However, their application to implicit generative models remains challenging due to the intractability of the likelihood function. To address this, we adapt a scoring rule posterior based on a strictly proper scoring rule, following the generalized Bayes framework. We then propose a block SGMCMC within Gibbs sampling mechanism. This enables efficient exploration of high-dimensional parameter spaces by identifying a sparse representation of neural implicit generative models. We demonstrate the performance of our proposed method through experiments on $p \gg n$ linear regression and an application of neural generative models.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a sample-efficient training mechanism for implicit generative models using shrinkage priors and generalized Bayes. It introduces a block SGMCMC within Gibbs sampling approach to explore high-dimensional parameter spaces and identify sparse representations of neural implicit generative models.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on $p \gg n$ linear regression and neural generative models, suggesting potential applicability to financial time series and alternative data where high-dimensional, sparse representations are common.
alpha_potential: The approach could be valuable for generating synthetic financial data or enhancing factor models by identifying sparse, meaningful patterns in high-dimensional financial datasets, potentially leading to more robust trading signals.
title_cn: 隐式生成模型的收缩先验
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于收缩先验和广义贝叶斯的样本高效训练机制，用于隐式生成模型。通过块SGMCMC吉布斯采样方法，探索高维参数空间并识别稀疏表示。在金融领域，该方法可应用于高维金融时间序列和另类数据，生成合成数据或增强因子模型，识别稀疏但有意义的模式，从而可能产生更稳健的交易信号。

title: Logarithmic Regret for Alternating Mirror Descent
summary: Alternating online mirror descent (AltOMD) is a simple learning rule for zero-sum games, which improves upon simultaneous OMD numerically and theoretically. Previous work obtained $O(T^{1/3})$ and $O(T^{1/5})$ regret bounds for AltOMD, by leveraging modified-energy-function-based analyses. However, settling whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret has remained an open question. In this paper we resolve the question of whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret in the affirmative. In particular, we show an $O(log(T))$ regret bound on the sum of the players' external regrets for any two-player zero-sum bilinear game with compact convex strategy sets, under mild regularity assumptions on the regularizers. We verify that our assumptions hold for the negative entropy regularizer, thereby obtaining logarithmic regret for the alternating multiplicative weights updates algorithm. The regret bound also yields an $O(log(T)/T)$ duality gap bound for the averaged strategies.
core_methodology: Alternating online mirror descent (AltOMD) for zero-sum games, achieving logarithmic regret bounds in two-player zero-sum bilinear games with compact convex strategy sets.
data_sources: Theoretical framework applicable to any financial market data where zero-sum game dynamics are relevant, such as options pricing or market making scenarios.
alpha_potential: Potential application in developing robust trading strategies in competitive environments (e.g., high-frequency trading or options markets) where game-theoretic considerations are important. The logarithmic regret bound suggests efficient adaptation to adversarial conditions.
title_cn: 交替镜像下降的对数遗憾
summary_cn: 本文提出的交替在线镜像下降(AltOMD)算法在零和博弈中实现了对数级遗憾界，适用于双人零和双线性博弈。该理论框架可应用于期权定价或做市等竞争性金融场景，为对抗环境下的交易策略提供理论基础。

title: On Discovering Algorithms for Adversarial Imitation Learning
summary: Adversarial Imitation Learning (AIL) methods, while effective in settings with limited expert demonstrations, are often considered unstable. These approaches typically decompose into two components: Density Ratio (DR) estimation $\frac{\rho_E}{\rho_{\pi}}$, where a discriminator estimates the relative occupancy of state-action pairs under the policy versus the expert; and Reward Assignment (RA), where this ratio is transformed into a reward signal used to train the policy. While significant research has focused on improving density estimation, the role of reward assignment in influencing training dynamics and final policy performance has been largely overlooked. RA functions in AIL are typically derived from divergence minimization objectives, relying heavily on human design and ingenuity. In this work, we take a different approach: we investigate the discovery of data-driven RA functions, i.e, based directly on the performance of the resulting imitation policy. To this end, we leverage an LLM-guided evolutionary framework that efficiently explores the space of RA functions, yielding \emph{Discovered Adversarial Imitation Learning} (DAIL), the first meta-learnt AIL algorithm. Remarkably, DAIL generalises across unseen environments and policy optimization algorithms, outperforming the current state-of-the-art of \emph{human-designed} baselines. Finally, we analyse why DAIL leads to more stable training, offering novel insights into the role of RA functions in the stability of AIL. Code is publicly available: https://github.com/shshnkreddy/DAIL.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Discovered Adversarial Imitation Learning (DAIL), a meta-learnt algorithm that uses an LLM-guided evolutionary framework to discover data-driven reward assignment functions for adversarial imitation learning. This approach improves the stability and performance of imitation learning by optimizing the reward assignment process based on the performance of the resulting imitation policy.
data_sources: The methodology is general and can be applied to any environment where expert demonstrations are available. In a financial context, this could include historical trading data, expert trader actions, or simulated market interactions.
alpha_potential: The approach could be adapted to develop trading strategies that mimic expert traders or optimal execution policies. The improved stability and generalization of DAIL could lead to more robust trading algorithms that perform well across different market conditions.
title_cn: 对抗性模仿学习算法的发现
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于LLM引导的进化框架的对抗性模仿学习算法（DAIL），通过数据驱动的奖励分配函数优化模仿策略的稳定性和性能。该方法可应用于金融领域，如开发模仿专家交易员的交易策略，提高算法在不同市场条件下的鲁棒性。

title: Tail reliability in probabilistic electricity price forecasts: comparing model combination and conformal prediction in the GB day-ahead market
summary: Probabilistic forecasts of day-ahead electricity prices are increasingly used to manage price risk, yet competing models are usually ranked on aggregate scores that average over the price regimes in which uncertainty matters most. This study evaluates probabilistic forecasts of hourly EPEX SPOT GB day-ahead prices over a full held-out calendar year, applying a common pre-auction information boundary and rolling-origin design to linear quantile regression, a quantile regression forest (QRF), a LEAR-QRA benchmark and an encoder-decoder quantile long short-term memory (LSTM) network. Two routes to more reliable intervals are then compared: conformal recalibration and Quantile Regression Averaging (QRA). Aggregate scores separate the LSTM and QRF only weakly, with a non-significant 4.4% difference in continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), but their conditional behaviour differs sharply. Above 200 GBP/MWh the LSTM covered 0.12 of outcomes and QRF 0.71, consistent with the forest retaining realised spikes in its leaf distributions while the network learned a smooth upper tail. Conformal recalibration corrected marginal coverage but did not improve the interval score or materially repair spike coverage. QRA combining the LSTM, QRF and LEAR-QRA forecasts reduced CRPS to 5.14 GBP/MWh and raised coverage above 200 GBP/MWh to 0.65 at unchanged interval width. Recalibration and combination therefore address different failures and are not substitutes.
core_methodology: The study compares probabilistic forecasting methods for electricity prices, specifically focusing on quantile regression models (linear quantile regression, quantile regression forest, LEAR-QRA) and an LSTM network. It evaluates two approaches to improve forecast reliability: conformal recalibration and Quantile Regression Averaging (QRA).
data_sources: Hourly EPEX SPOT GB day-ahead electricity prices over a full held-out calendar year, using a common pre-auction information boundary and rolling-origin design.
alpha_potential: The study highlights the potential for improved probabilistic forecasts in volatile price regimes (e.g., price spikes above 200 GBP/MWh), which could be valuable for risk management and trading strategies in electricity markets. The combination of LSTM, QRF, and LEAR-QRA forecasts via QRA showed improved performance metrics (CRPS and coverage).
title_cn: 概率电价预测中的尾部可靠性：GB日前市场中模型组合与保形预测的比较
summary_cn: 本研究对比了多种概率预测模型（包括分位数回归、QRF和LSTM）在GB日前电价预测中的表现，并评估了保形重新校准和分位数回归平均（QRA）两种方法。研究发现QRA组合方法能显著提高高价格区间的覆盖率，对电力市场交易和风险管理具有潜在应用价值。

title: UniFlow: Unified Multi-Scale Flow Matching for Time Series Generation
summary: Real-world time series exhibit complex dynamics across multiple temporal resolutions, yet effectively incorporating multi-scale information into generative modeling remains challenging without increasing generative complexity. We propose UniFlow, a unified framework that integrates multi-scale representation learning with efficient non-autoregressive generation through a shared-semantic discrete interface. Specifically, a multi-scale tokenizer employs shared-index voting to consolidate complementary temporal information into a single public-ID sequence, while scale-specific codebooks preserve the information required for reconstruction. Building on this unified representation, we develop geometry-aware categorical flow matching, which initializes transport from learned low-rank anchors and generates public identities non-autoregressively. This design captures multi-scale temporal structure without requiring multiple generative token streams or sequential token decoding. Experiments across four benchmarks and both short- and long-term settings demonstrate improved generative fidelity, strong cross-scale consistency, and substantial inference speedups over representative autoregressive and diffusion-based baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/William-Liwei/uniflow
core_methodology: UniFlow integrates multi-scale representation learning with efficient non-autoregressive generation through a shared-semantic discrete interface. It uses a multi-scale tokenizer with shared-index voting to consolidate temporal information and scale-specific codebooks for reconstruction. The method employs geometry-aware categorical flow matching for non-autoregressive generation.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method across four benchmarks in both short- and long-term settings, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to capture multi-scale temporal structure efficiently could be leveraged for generating synthetic financial time series or enhancing predictive models in trading strategies, particularly in high-frequency trading where multi-scale information is crucial.
title_cn: UniFlow：统一多尺度流匹配用于时间序列生成
summary_cn: UniFlow提出了一种统一框架，通过共享语义离散接口整合多尺度表示学习与非自回归生成，能高效捕捉多尺度时间结构。该方法在四个基准测试中表现出色，适用于高频交易中多尺度时间序列的生成与预测。

title: Scalable and adaptive prediction bands with kernel sum-of-squares
summary: Conformal Prediction (CP) is a popular framework for constructing prediction bands with valid coverage in finite samples, while being free of any distributional assumption. A well-known limitation of conformal prediction is the lack of adaptivity, although several works introduced practically efficient alternate procedures. In this work, we build upon recent ideas that rely on recasting the CP problem as a statistical learning problem, directly targeting coverage and adaptivity. This statistical learning problem is based on reproducible kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS) and kernel sum-of-squares (SoS) methods. First, we extend previous results with a general representer theorem and exhibit the dual formulation of the learning problem. Crucially, such dual formulation can be solved efficiently by accelerated gradient methods with several hundreds or thousands of samples, unlike previous strategies based on off-the-shelf semidefinite programming algorithms. Second, we introduce a new hyperparameter tuning strategy tailored specifically to target adaptivity through bounds on test-conditional coverage. This strategy, based on the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC), is introduced here to tune kernel lengthscales in our framework, but has broader applicability since it could be used in any CP algorithm where the score function is learned. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted to show how our method compares to related work. All figures can be reproduced with the accompanying code at \href{https://www.gitlab.com/drti/ksos-bands}{gitlab.com/drti/ksos-bands}.
core_methodology: The paper presents a method for constructing prediction bands using kernel sum-of-squares (SoS) within the Conformal Prediction (CP) framework. It introduces a dual formulation that can be solved efficiently by accelerated gradient methods and proposes a hyperparameter tuning strategy based on the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) for targeting adaptivity.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources but the methodology is applicable to any dataset suitable for conformal prediction, which could include financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be used to construct robust prediction intervals for financial time series, which may enhance risk management and trading strategy development by providing more adaptive and accurate uncertainty estimates.
title_cn: 可扩展且自适应的预测带与核平方和方法
summary_cn: 该研究通过核平方和方法改进了共形预测框架，提出了高效的双重优化方法和基于HSIC的超参数调优策略，能够生成更自适应的预测带。在量化交易中，该方法可用于提高金融时间序列预测的准确性及不确定性估计，从而辅助风险管理与策略优化。

title: A mathematical study of the excess growth rate
summary: The excess growth rate, defined as the gap in Jensen's inequality for the logarithm, is a fundamental functional in portfolio theory. In this paper, we present a mathematical study motivated by information theory. We begin by establishing its properties and showing that it has rich connections with information-theoretic concepts such as the Helmholtz free energy, L. Campbell's measure of average code length and large deviations. Our main results consist of three axiomatic characterization theorems of the excess growth rate, in terms of (i) the relative entropy, (ii) the gap in Jensen's inequality, and (iii) the logarithmic divergence that generalizes the Bregman divergence. Furthermore, we study maximization of the excess growth rate and compare it with Kelly's growth optimal portfolio. Our results not only provide theoretical justifications of the significance of the excess growth rate, but also establish new connections between information theory and quantitative finance.
core_methodology: Mathematical study of the excess growth rate, focusing on its properties and connections with information-theoretic concepts, including axiomatic characterizations and maximization techniques.
data_sources: Theoretical, no specific market data mentioned but applicable to portfolio returns data.
alpha_potential: Potential for improving portfolio optimization strategies by better understanding and utilizing the excess growth rate, particularly in comparison to Kelly's growth optimal portfolio.
title_cn: 超额增长率数学研究
summary_cn: 本文对超额增长率进行了数学研究，探讨了其与信息论概念的联系，并提出了三种公理化特征定理。研究结果不仅为超额增长率的重要性提供了理论依据，还为信息论与量化金融之间建立了新的联系，对投资组合优化策略具有潜在应用价值。

title: Rethinking the Unsupervised Paradigm in Time Series Anomaly Detection: An Empirical Study and Minimalist Baseline
summary: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) research predominantly focuses on unsupervised architectures to model normal data dynamics under label scarcity. However, practical deployments frequently archive historical operational incidents, questioning whether continuous unsupervised architectural scaling remains the most cost-effective pursuit. In this paper, we empirically quantify the trade-offs between supervisory signals and model complexity. We introduce STAND, a deliberately minimalist supervised baseline based on bidirectional recurrent encoding. Across five benchmark datasets evaluated under a strictly disjoint out-of-sample temporal protocol, minimalist supervised models achieve competitive or superior accuracy relative to complex unsupervised alternatives. Furthermore, controlled label-scaling and few-shot evaluations confirm that these supervisory advantages persist under constrained historical event budgets, while STAND exhibits higher prediction certainty and sharper event delineation than reconstruction-based baselines. These findings encourage the TSAD community to complement algorithmic complexity with data-centric label utilization when annotations are accessible. The source code, benchmark datasets, and an extended Supplementary Document are publicly available at https://emorzz1g.github.io/STAND.
core_methodology: The paper introduces STAND, a minimalist supervised baseline for time series anomaly detection (TSAD) using bidirectional recurrent encoding. It empirically compares supervised and unsupervised approaches, demonstrating that supervised methods can achieve competitive or superior accuracy even with limited labeled data.
data_sources: The study evaluates performance across five benchmark datasets, though the specific datasets are not detailed in the abstract. These likely include standard TSAD datasets from operational or industrial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to detect anomalies in financial time series (e.g., price movements, order flow, or volatility patterns), potentially identifying rare events or regime shifts that precede market opportunities. The supervised approach may offer sharper event delineation than unsupervised methods, which could improve signal precision.
title_cn: 重新思考时间序列异常检测中的无监督范式：实证研究与极简基线
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种极简监督基线STAND，用于时间序列异常检测。研究表明，即使标注数据有限，监督方法也能达到或超越复杂无监督模型的性能。这一方法可应用于金融市场异常检测（如价格突变或流动性变化），为量化交易提供更精确的事件信号。

title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning via a Poisson-Moreau Drift
summary: Establishing almost sure convergence rates for stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning under Markovian noise is a fundamental theoretical challenge. We make progress towards this challenge for a class of stochastic approximation algorithms whose expected updates are contractive, a setting that arises in many reinforcement learning algorithms such as $Q$-learning and linear temporal difference learning. Specifically, for a power-law learning rate $O(n^{-\eta})$ with $\eta \in (1/2, 1)$, we obtain an almost sure convergence rate arbitrarily close to $o(n^{1 - 2\eta})$. For the harmonic learning rate $\alpha_n=\alpha/(n+1)$, the almost sure squared-error rate is $o(n^{-\zeta})$ for every $\zeta<\min\{1,2(1-\kappa)\alpha\}$, where $\kappa$ is the contraction factor. Thus exponents arbitrarily close to one are available when $2(1-\kappa)\alpha\geq1$. This approaches the $n^{-1}$ polynomial exponent of classical law-of-the-iterated-logarithm benchmarks. Key to our analysis is a novel Lyapunov drift construction that applies a Poisson-equation based correction for Markovian noise to the well-established Moreau-envelope smoothing for the contractive mapping.
core_methodology: The paper presents a novel Lyapunov drift construction for analyzing stochastic approximation algorithms under Markovian noise, specifically applying Poisson-equation based correction and Moreau-envelope smoothing to contractive mappings. This methodology is particularly relevant for reinforcement learning algorithms like Q-learning and temporal difference learning.
data_sources: Theoretical analysis does not specify particular data sources but is applicable to any financial data that can be modeled with Markovian noise, such as price series or order book data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could improve the convergence rates of reinforcement learning algorithms used in trading strategy optimization, potentially leading to more efficient learning of optimal trading policies in dynamic markets. However, the practical implementation and empirical validation in financial contexts would be required to realize this potential.

title: Robust Learning under Non-Gaussian Noise with Adaptive Log-Correntropy Loss
summary: Robust deep learning under heavy-tailed and impulsive noise remains challenging because conventional losses such as mean squared error (MSE) exhibit unbounded sensitivity to outliers. Although correntropy-based objectives improve robustness, many conventional formulations rely on fixed kernel parameters that must be empirically tuned and remain static during training. To address these limitations, we propose an Adaptive Log-Correntropy Loss (ALCL), a heavy-tailed loss formulation that adaptively learns its robustness geometry during optimization. ALCL introduces a logarithmic residual model whose shape and scale parameters are learned jointly with network weights through differentiable reparameterization. This yields a heavy-tailed robust optimization objective whose psi-function is formally bounded and redescending, allowing the loss geometry to adapt dynamically to evolving residual statistics while suppressing extreme outliers. Comparative experiments on four widely used benchmark datasets spanning grayscale and red-green-blue (RGB) image data under mixed heavy-tailed and impulsive noise demonstrate that ALCL consistently outperforms MSE and optimally tuned generalized correntropy losses in both reconstruction fidelity and downstream classification accuracy. While performance differences remain small under low-noise conditions, under high-noise regimes ALCL improves median accuracy by up to 4.75% on grayscale benchmarks and 4.51% on RGB datasets, with reduced variance across runs. These results demonstrate that adaptive robustness through joint learning of loss parameters provides a computationally efficient alternative to static correntropy-based losses for deep learning in non-Gaussian environments.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an Adaptive Log-Correntropy Loss (ALCL) for robust deep learning under heavy-tailed and impulsive noise. ALCL adaptively learns its robustness geometry during optimization, making it suitable for non-Gaussian environments.
data_sources: The paper uses four widely used benchmark datasets spanning grayscale and RGB image data under mixed heavy-tailed and impulsive noise.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for financial time series data, which often exhibits heavy-tailed and non-Gaussian noise. The adaptive nature of ALCL could improve the robustness of trading models in volatile or outlier-rich market conditions.

title: Sparse stochastic digital twins can outperform exact ones
summary: Digital twins are often built under the assumption that greater model fidelity leads to better downstream performance. We show that this is not always the case: retaining weakly dependent or auxiliary degrees of freedom can increase the dimensionality of learning and control problems enough that a sparse stochastic surrogate outperforms even an exact high-dimensional model. To identify such structure, we introduce a framework for dependence discovery directly at the level of the full conditional law. The method combines conditional generative modeling with Gaussian-process distillation and kernel mode decomposition to quantify how strongly individual variables enter the conditional distribution, including through variability, tails, multimodality, and other features invisible to the conditional mean. The resulting dependence structure can be used both to construct sparse stochastic digital twins from data and to reduce known high-dimensional models for downstream tasks. In a modified Lunar Lander problem, an eight-dimensional sparse surrogate yields better control performance than the exact 109-dimensional simulator despite lower transition fidelity. A stochastic heat-equation example shows that the framework recovers sparse structure in a 102-dimensional data-driven setting and produces a more effective surrogate than one conditioned on all candidate inputs, while economic data demonstrate its use for identifying time-varying memory structure. These results show that model fidelity and downstream utility are distinct objectives, and that dependence discovery provides a practical route to sparse stochastic digital twins.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a framework for dependence discovery at the level of the full conditional law, combining conditional generative modeling with Gaussian-process distillation and kernel mode decomposition. This methodology identifies sparse structure in high-dimensional models, enabling the construction of sparse stochastic digital twins that can outperform exact high-dimensional models in downstream tasks.
data_sources: The paper uses synthetic data from a modified Lunar Lander problem, a stochastic heat-equation example, and economic data to demonstrate the framework's effectiveness.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to financial markets to identify sparse, high-impact variables in complex datasets, potentially improving predictive models and trading strategies by focusing on the most relevant dependencies and reducing noise from weakly dependent variables.

title: Does Source-Free Time-Series Adaptation Really Require Updating the Encoder?
summary: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) adapts a pretrained model to an unlabeled target domain without accessing source data, enabling the reuse of time-series predictors across sensing systems. Existing methods commonly update the encoder using unlabeled target objectives. Yet changes in users, equipment, and operating conditions also alter the spectral characteristics of input signals, raising a fundamental question: does adaptation require changing the encoder, or can we instead adapt the signal it receives? We propose Source Free Frequency-Prototype Alignment (SF-FPA), which learns a spectral input transformation while freezing the source encoder and classifier parameters. First, a frequency adaptation layer applies amplitude and phase corrections to target signals. Separate branches adjust spectral magnitudes and phase relationships, with circular phase encoding avoiding discontinuities at the angular boundary. Second, confidence-filtered prototype alignment guides target representations toward source class prototypes. Combined with information maximization, this objective propagates gradients through the source predictor to learn spectral corrections that support class discrimination. Extensive experiments on three real-world time series benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art average Macro-F1 performance. Component ablations and controlled comparisons with encoder adaptation and a parameter-matched time-domain adapter further support spectral input adaptation as an effective approach to reusing source-trained predictors. The implementation is available at https://github.com/ShichangMeng/SF_FPA.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Source Free Frequency-Prototype Alignment (SF-FPA), a method for adapting pretrained models to new domains without accessing the original training data. It focuses on adjusting the spectral characteristics of input signals (amplitude and phase corrections) while keeping the encoder and classifier frozen, using confidence-filtered prototype alignment and information maximization.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on three real-world time series benchmarks, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned. The approach is general and could be applied to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to financial time series data to improve model robustness across different market regimes or instruments without retraining, potentially capturing regime shifts or adapting to new asset classes more effectively.

title: An Efficient Minimax-Optimal Algorithm for Adversarial $m$-Set Bandits
summary: We study adversarial combinatorial bandits with $m$-set actions, where at each round the learner selects $m$ out of $d$ items and observes only the aggregate loss of the selected items. The resulting action set contains $K=\binom{d}{m}$ elements and can therefore be exponentially large. We propose a computationally efficient algorithm that exploits this structure without explicitly enumerating the action set. Against adaptive non-anticipating adversaries, it guarantees, with probability at least $1-\delta$, regret against the best action in hindsight of $R_T =O(\sqrt{dT\log(K/\delta)}). $ This matches the high-probability regret bound of the finite-action EXP3 with Kiefer-Wolfowitz exploration algorithm of Zimmert and Lattimore, whose direct implementation may require exponential space. Our algorithm instead represents each sampling distribution with $d$ parameters and runs in polynomial time without enumerating the action set. This resolves an open problem posed by Maiti et al. We complement this upper bound with a matching high-probability lower bound. For all sufficiently small $\delta$ and all sufficiently large horizons, every randomized algorithm admits an adaptive non-anticipating adversary for which, with probability at least $\delta$, $R_T=\Omega( \sqrt{dT\log(K/\delta)}). $ Thus, the rate is minimax optimal up to universal constants in this regime. In particular, setting $m=1$ shows that the $\log K$ factor in the high-probability regret bound for ordinary $K$-armed bandits against adaptive non-anticipating adversaries is unavoidable. This strengthens the lower bound of Gerchinovitz and Lattimore, closing the remaining $\sqrt{\log K}$ gap between high-probability upper and lower regret bounds.
core_methodology: The paper presents an efficient algorithm for adversarial combinatorial bandits with m-set actions, which avoids the exponential complexity of enumerating all possible actions by representing sampling distributions with d parameters and running in polynomial time.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to scenarios where the learner selects m out of d items and observes aggregate losses, which could be analogous to selecting a subset of assets in a portfolio.
alpha_potential: The algorithm's ability to efficiently handle large action spaces and provide minimax-optimal regret bounds could be valuable for portfolio optimization and adaptive trading strategies where the action space is combinatorially large.

title: A Concentration Bound for Two-Timescale Actor-Critic Algorithm
summary: Significant research effort has been directed in recent years towards establishing both asymptotic and non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for two-timescale actor--critic algorithms, where the actor recursion is run on a slower timescale than the critic recursion. This work derives a uniform all-time concentration bound for the actor--critic algorithm with function approximation in the long-run average-reward setting. This bound helps us analyze the behavior of the actor parameter with high probability. We show that, after some finite time, the actor parameter enters a safe region and remains within it thereafter with high probability. Specifically, with probability at least $1-\epsilon_1-\epsilon_2$, the actor error $\Vert \theta_k-\theta^{*}\Vert$ is $O\left(\frac{n_0^{3/4}}{k}\frac{1}{\sqrt{\epsilon_2}}+\left(\frac{1}{n_0}\right)^{1/4}\log^{1/4}\left(\frac{1}{\epsilon_1}\right)+\left(\frac{1}{n_0}\right)^{1/4}\right)$ for all $k\geq n_0$ and sufficiently large $n_0$. We also present experimental results demonstrating that the aforementioned actor error diminishes with the number of actor-parameter updates.
core_methodology: The paper presents a two-timescale actor-critic algorithm with function approximation, focusing on deriving uniform concentration bounds for the actor parameter in the long-run average-reward setting. The analysis provides high-probability guarantees on the actor parameter's convergence to a safe region.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is general and could be applied to financial time series data for reinforcement learning-based trading strategies.
alpha_potential: The theoretical guarantees on the actor-critic algorithm's convergence could be valuable for developing robust reinforcement learning-based trading strategies, particularly in environments where policy stability is crucial. The high-probability bounds may help in designing more reliable algorithmic trading systems.

title: Bayesian Optimization with Fisher Information Geometry: Gradient Bounds and Trust-Region Methods
summary: We study Bayesian optimization (BO) through the lens of information geometry. Pulling back the Fisher information metric through the surrogate posterior map yields a local sensitivity tensor on the input space, which leads to an upper bound on the gradient of reparameterizable acquisition functions (AFs). This view explains vanishing-gradient behavior in high-dimensional BO and provides a common interpretation of heuristics such as RAASP and dimension-scaled lengthscales. The upper bound can also serve as a generic recipe to understand the behavior of new acquisition functions or surrogates in high input dimensions as well. Using the bounds, we also identify necessary conditions for an input location to be an optimizer of the AF for a univariate Gaussian predictive posterior. Building on this analysis, we propose FITR, a trust-region-based BO method that replaces lengthscale-based scaling with local pullback-Fisher weights. FITR is not restricted to GP kernels with explicit lengthscales and easily generalizes to non-isotropic surrogates. FITR shows competitive performance on several benchmarks.
core_methodology: The paper presents Bayesian optimization (BO) with Fisher information geometry, focusing on gradient bounds and trust-region methods. It introduces a local sensitivity tensor derived from the Fisher information metric to improve BO performance, particularly in high dimensions.
data_sources: Benchmark datasets for Bayesian optimization (unspecified financial datasets).
alpha_potential: The method could enhance parameter tuning in trading strategies or portfolio optimization by providing more robust and efficient search mechanisms. It may help in identifying optimal hyperparameters for machine learning models used in trading.

summary_cn: 该研究通过Fisher信息几何改进贝叶斯优化，引入了局部敏感张量以解决高维优化中的梯度消失问题。FITR方法通过局部Fisher权重替代传统长度尺度，适用于非各向同性代理模型。在量化交易中，可用于优化策略参数或机器学习模型超参数，提升搜索效率。

title: Lotus: Learning to Understand Time-series by Learning to Forecast
summary: Time-series language models typically align numerical signals with language using labels, captions, or question-answer pairs, without explicitly requiring their representations to preserve how the underlying signals evolve. We introduce forecast grounding, a pretraining principle that requires language-aligned time-series representations to remain predictive of the future evolution before they are adapted to downstream tasks. We instantiate this principle in Lotus, which divides each time-series channel into non-overlapping patches and maps them into the LLM embedding space. It then predicts the next patch from the LLM hidden states of the time-series tokens, encouraging the learned representation to retain temporal information. To capture both temporal changes and periodic patterns, we also propose a temporal-spectral patch representation that combines each raw time-series patch with its spectral representation before mapping it into the LLM embedding space. Across three language model backbones and six downstream evaluation datasets, Lotus achieves the best average performance with minimal trainable parameters, reaching 59.91% accuracy and outperforming the strongest matched baseline by 3.36%. Our representation analyses further show that Lotus uses the numerical input and preserves temporal structure in its learned patch representations. These results establish forecast grounding as a promising pretraining principle, enabling compact time-series language models to outperform models 25-50 times their size on TSRBench. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/DA2I2-SLM/Lotus
core_methodology: Lotus introduces forecast grounding, a pretraining principle that requires language-aligned time-series representations to predict future evolution before being adapted to downstream tasks. It divides time-series channels into non-overlapping patches, maps them into the LLM embedding space, and predicts the next patch from the hidden states. Additionally, it uses a temporal-spectral patch representation to capture both temporal changes and periodic patterns.
data_sources: The paper does not specify exact financial datasets but mentions evaluation across six downstream datasets, suggesting potential applicability to market time-series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to financial time-series forecasting, potentially identifying predictive patterns in market data that are not captured by traditional models. The preservation of temporal structure in learned representations could enhance predictive accuracy in trading signals.
title_cn: Lotus：通过学习预测来理解时间序列

title: MAS-Loop: Beyond One-Shot Orchestration towards Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Training-time multi-agent system (MAS) design seeks to learn reusable orchestration policies, yet prevailing approaches remain largely one-shot: an Orchestrator generates a system but only observes and learns from its terminal outcome. This paradigm discards execution trajectories that expose system-level failures and contain fine-grained information beyond the terminal outcome, leaving no direct basis for revising the source MAS, evaluating the updated MAS, or learning from the resulting contrast. To this end, we introduce MAS-Loop, an execution-grounded framework that closes this feedback loop by coupling an Orchestrator with a trajectory-conditioned Refiner. For each task, the Orchestrator constructs and executes a source MAS to obtain an outcome score and an intermediate trajectory. Conditioned on the trajectory, the Refiner localizes an actionable failure, formulates a trajectory-grounded diagnosis, and proposes a bounded patch to the agents, information flow, or execution configuration. The executable updated MAS is re-executed on the same task to measure its realized outcome under stochastic execution. This pair-MAS comparison provides complementary learning signals: the Orchestrator learns to generate strong systems with fewer recoverable failures, whereas the Refiner learns to expose and repair observed weaknesses, thereby driving policy-level co-evolution across training iterations. Experiments show that MAS-Loop achieves the strongest overall performance among the evaluated baselines, with consistent gains from refinement across all evaluated benchmarks. The co-evolution process also yields MAS-JudgeCorpus, a dataset of execution-grounded source-updated pairs with orchestration- and trajectory-level supervision, which can provide the community with support for MAS reward modeling and trajectory-aware investigation.
core_methodology: Execution-grounded framework for multi-agent system refinement through iterative learning from execution trajectories
data_sources: Self-generated execution trajectories from MAS operations (not financial market data)
alpha_potential: Potential to optimize trading agent ensembles through continuous refinement and failure analysis, though not directly demonstrated on financial applications

title: Quantile Propagation Planning for Budgeted Tail-Risk Evaluation
summary: Risk-aware planning must identify rare, costly outcomes using only a limited number of model evaluations. Monte Carlo rollouts spend this budget on noisy tail estimates, while planning from the mean can miss the tail entirely. We introduce quantile propagation planning (QPP), which propagates a small, fixed set of disturbance quantiles through the dynamics and integrates the resulting cost curve to evaluate both mean and tail risk. The method is exact at the propagated levels, converges as the quantile grid is refined, and admits a one-sided conservatism guarantee under stated structural conditions. In controlled overload and inventory tasks, QPP reduces realized tail cost and constraint violations relative to mean-rollout planning. On overload, it remains competitive with sampled evaluators that use substantially more trajectories. These results position QPP as a transparent, budget-controlled approach to tail-risk evaluation.
core_methodology: Quantile propagation planning (QPP) is introduced as a method to evaluate both mean and tail risk by propagating a fixed set of disturbance quantiles through the dynamics and integrating the resulting cost curve. This approach provides exact estimates at propagated levels and converges as the quantile grid is refined, with a one-sided conservatism guarantee under certain structural conditions.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any scenario where risk-aware planning is needed, such as financial markets where tail-risk evaluation is crucial.
alpha_potential: QPP's ability to accurately evaluate tail risks with limited computational resources could be valuable in portfolio optimization and risk management, particularly in strategies that require robust handling of rare but costly market events. This could lead to better risk-adjusted returns by avoiding or mitigating tail risks more effectively than traditional methods.
title_cn: 基于预算的尾部风险评估的分位数传播规划
summary_cn: 本文提出的分位数传播规划（QPP）方法通过传播一组固定的扰动分位数来评估均值和尾部风险，适用于需要精确尾部风险评估的金融场景。在投资组合优化和风险管理中，QPP能够以有限的计算资源有效识别和处理罕见但高成本的市场事件，从而提升风险调整后的收益。

title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
summary: Agentic workflows are increasingly shifting towards long-horizon tasks, such as open-ended scientific work, where models benefit from long context windows. However, at ultra-long context (above 1M tokens), full attention is prohibitively expensive. A promising approach is sparse attention, in which a dedicated indexer selects a subset of keys for the attention. Yet current methods of indexing either still have quadratic cost in context size or lose accuracy at ultra-long context scale. We address this with Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), an efficient attention method that maintains accuracy at ultra-long context. In LSA, keys are hierarchically clustered in a learned latent space, and queries score the hierarchy of clusters instead of scoring every key, making prefill, decode and training faster at long context. We propose two variants, Distilled-LSA (D-LSA), which can be applied to pre-trained models via distillation, and Native-LSA (N-LSA), which is trained natively on the next-token loss alone. On GLM-5.3-FLASH (QWEN-3.8-27B) at 10M tokens, D-LSA speeds up one attention layer by 22.7x (72.4x) in prefill and 4.6x (42.5x) in decode over its original sparse attention (full attention), while keeping similar accuracy across a variety of tasks. N-LSA matches the accuracy of full attention with a training speedup of 1.6x per layer at 128k tokens. LSA offers practical and efficient attention for models to benefit from ultra-long context.
core_methodology: Latent Sparse Attention (LSA) is an efficient attention method that hierarchically clusters keys in a learned latent space, allowing queries to score clusters instead of individual keys. This reduces computational complexity from quadratic to subquadratic, making it feasible to process ultra-long contexts (up to 10M tokens). Two variants are proposed: Distilled-LSA (D-LSA) for pre-trained models and Native-LSA (N-LSA) for models trained from scratch.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, but the methodology is general and could be applied to sequential financial data such as high-frequency tick data, order books, or long historical price series.
alpha_potential: The ability to process ultra-long contexts efficiently could enable new trading strategies that leverage very long-term dependencies in market data, such as detecting multi-scale patterns or integrating diverse information sources over extended time horizons. This could be particularly valuable for macro trading, event-driven strategies, or complex multi-asset strategies.

summary_cn: 该研究提出的潜在稀疏注意力（LSA）通过层次化聚类和潜在空间学习，实现了对超长上下文（千万级token）的高效处理，计算复杂度从二次降至次二次。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于处理超长金融时间序列，挖掘多尺度市场规律，或整合跨资产、跨市场的长期关联信号，为基于深度学习的宏观交易或复杂事件驱动策略提供技术支持。

title: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen
summary: Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? As candidate targets are numerous in enterprise settings, it is preferable to avoid learning a new model from scratch each time there is a new prediction task. Frozen foundation models (FMs) based on in-context learning (ICL) and RDB-specific pre-training provide a viable solution, but the ideal design still remains largely unresolved. Perhaps unexpectedly, preliminary evidence has recently shown that existing single-table FMs (aka TFMs), when combined with suitable parameter-free relational encoders, can be quite competitive in practice despite zero exposure to RDB pre-training or relational data of any kind. In this work we first empirically confirm this phenomenon with a more diverse array of experiments. We then turn to our main contribution, namely, surfacing multiple complementary explanations for why TFMs behave so effectively. These explanations ultimately hinge on innate synergies whereby parameter-free encoders map relational effects to fixed-length embeddings that loosely mimic distributions for which TFMs were originally designed; in so doing, desirable single-table properties transfer to relational settings (e.g., convergent posterior predictive distributions). Collectively, our analysis forges new pathways for improving RDB FMs, particularly when we prioritize interpretability and inevitable integration within agentic systems.
core_methodology: The paper explores the use of frozen foundation models (FMs) with in-context learning (ICL) and relational encoders for predicting missing or future values in relational databases. It focuses on how single-table foundation models (TFMs) can be effectively applied to relational data without specific pre-training.
data_sources: Relational databases (RDBs) storing heterogeneous tabular information, which could be analogous to financial datasets like market data, fundamental data, or alternative data structured in tables.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to predict missing financial data or future values in time-series datasets, potentially uncovering hidden patterns or signals in structured financial data. However, direct application to trading strategies would require significant adaptation and validation.
title_cn: 为何表格基础模型在未见过的关系数据上表现优异
summary_cn: 本研究探讨了如何利用冻结的基础模型和关系编码器预测关系数据库中的缺失或未来值。尽管模型未经过特定预训练，但通过参数无关的编码器将关系效应映射到固定长度嵌入，单表属性可迁移到关系设置。该方法可能适用于金融数据的缺失值预测或时间序列分析，但需进一步适配以用于实际交易策略。

title: From Individual Learning to Market Equilibrium: Correcting Structural and Parametric Biases in RL Simulations of Economic Models
summary: Applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to economic modeling reveals a fundamental tension: standard RL agents do not behave as competitive price-takers. While macroeconomic models typically assume agents take aggregate conditions as given, a naive single-agent RL algorithm learns to internalize its impact on the environment, effectively exerting market power. We illustrate this divergence in a search-and-matching model with concave production, showing that a standard RL agent converges to a monopsonistic allocation rather than the competitive equilibrium. Furthermore, we show that RL's approach to time discounting distorts standard intertemporal economic trade-offs. To resolve these issues, we propose a Calibrated Mean-Field Reinforcement Learning framework that restricts the agent to optimize against an exogenous aggregate state to restore price-taking behavior, and recalibrates the RL reward structure to reflect true economic opportunity costs. By iteratively updating the aggregate state, our algorithm converges to a stationary fixed point that recovers the competitive equilibrium. This approach provides a method for embedding learning algorithms into dynamic general equilibrium models.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a Calibrated Mean-Field Reinforcement Learning framework to address the divergence between standard RL agents and competitive price-taking behavior in economic models. It involves restricting agents to optimize against an exogenous aggregate state and recalibrating reward structures.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on a search-and-matching model with concave production, which is a theoretical economic model rather than real-market data.
alpha_potential: The approach could potentially be adapted to simulate market conditions where algorithmic traders need to account for their market impact while maintaining competitive behavior, possibly improving execution strategies or market-making algorithms.
title_cn: 从个体学习到市场均衡：纠正经济模型RL模拟中的结构和参数偏差
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种校准的平均场强化学习框架，解决了标准RL算法在模拟经济模型时与竞争性价格接受行为之间的偏差。对于量化交易，该方法可应用于改进执行策略或做市算法，尤其是在考虑市场影响的情况下保持竞争行为。

title: A Financial Brain Scan of the LLM
summary: We use sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to "brain scan" large language models, mapping internal activations to interpretable concepts and enabling targeted "steering" of specific features. We show that prompting models to adopt specific preferences activates many unintended concepts, complicating causal inference. In contrast, SAEs permit smooth, more isolated steering of target concepts. Furthermore, our scans reveal a stark disconnect between the model's internal feature contributions and its self-generated explanations, showing that these explanations are unreliable guides to its reasoning. Finally, SAEs provide a lightweight intervention for existing models, producing interpretable embeddings and allowing researchers to attenuate specific economic biases.
core_methodology: The paper uses sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to analyze and interpret the internal activations of large language models (LLMs), enabling targeted steering of specific features and concepts. This approach allows for more isolated and controlled manipulation of model behavior compared to traditional prompting methods.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but focuses on the internal activations and feature contributions within LLMs, which could theoretically be applied to financial text data or market sentiment analysis.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to identify and mitigate biases in financial LLMs, potentially improving the reliability of model-generated trading signals or sentiment analysis. The ability to 'steer' specific features might also allow for more precise control over model outputs in trading strategies.
title_cn: 大型语言模型的金融脑扫描
summary_cn: 本研究利用稀疏自编码器（SAE）对大型语言模型（LLM）进行‘脑扫描’，映射内部激活到可解释的概念，并实现对特定特征的有针对性的‘引导’。这种方法可以更平滑、更孤立地操控目标概念，相比传统提示方法更可靠。研究发现模型内部特征贡献与其自我生成的解释之间存在明显脱节，表明这些解释不可靠。SAE提供了一种轻量级干预，可用于减轻特定经济偏见，可能提升金融LLM在交易策略中的可靠性。

title: Quantification of Tail-trimming Effects for Interval CVaR Based Nonlinear Regression
summary: The tail trimming strategy is widely adopted for robustness against outlier contamination in statistical learning and operations research. However, it generally lacks the thorough understanding that to what extent the tail-trimming technique is effective for nonlinear regression. In this paper, we address the robust nonlinear regression based on the so-called interval conditional value-at-risk (In-CVaR), which is introduced to guard against outliers by trimming extreme losses. We first analyze the trimming effect of the In-CVaR based estimator under distributional perturbation. Our first finding is that the In-CVaR based estimator is qualitatively robust under distributional perturbation in terms of the Prokhorov metric if and only if the largest portion of losses is trimmed. Furthermore, under sample contamination, we derive a probably approximately correct (PAC) bound for the In-CVaR based estimator, showing that the preliminary covariate filtering that is customary in the literature is not needed for In-CVaR based regression. The nonconvexity of the In-CVaR objective, together with unboundedness of covariates, responses and parameter space create the technical challenges for our developed theory, and thus necessitate the new treatment of the qualitative robustness and PAC analysis. Overall, this study rigorously analyzes robustness properties of In-CVaR based nonlinear regression models, which illustrates to what extent the right tail-trimming of the loss by In-CVaR risk measure is essential and effective for robust nonlinear regression. These theoretical findings are further supported by numerical experiments.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on robust nonlinear regression using interval conditional value-at-risk (In-CVaR) to mitigate the effects of outliers through tail-trimming strategies. It provides theoretical analysis of the robustness properties and PAC bounds under distributional perturbation and sample contamination.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any financial datasets involving nonlinear regression, such as asset returns or risk factors.
alpha_potential: The In-CVaR based estimator could potentially improve the robustness of factor models or risk management strategies by effectively trimming extreme losses, which may lead to more stable and reliable performance in the presence of outliers.

title: Optimal Value Inference for Reinforcement Learning
summary: We study offline inference for the optimal value in reinforcement learning under finite state and action spaces. Two new nuisances are derived as fixed points of a self-induced Bellman equation, in which we approximate the maximum Bellman operator by its softmax correspondence. We propose a debiased estimator through the Neyman orthogonality and establish its asymptotic normality under diverging horizons even when the behavior policy changes with time, as long as the nuisances have the statistical rates that can be achieved by many machine learning methods. We provide a concrete estimating procedure for these nuisances and show they can lead to valid inference. Synthetic experiments validate the numerical performance of our inference method, and we implement it in real-life decision-making problems, including bike repositioning and AI agentic tool use.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a debiased estimator for optimal value inference in reinforcement learning, utilizing a softmax approximation of the maximum Bellman operator and Neyman orthogonality for asymptotic normality. The method is validated through synthetic experiments and real-life applications like bike repositioning.
data_sources: The abstract mentions synthetic experiments and real-life applications, but specific financial data sources are not detailed. Potential applications could use historical market data or alternative datasets relevant to trading strategies.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to develop reinforcement learning-based trading strategies, particularly in portfolio optimization or dynamic asset allocation, by inferring optimal values from historical data. The debiased estimator might help in reducing bias in value estimates, potentially leading to more robust trading signals.
title_cn: 强化学习中的最优值推断
summary_cn: 本文研究离线强化学习中的最优值推断，提出了一种基于自诱导贝尔曼方程和软最大近似的去偏估计方法，并建立了其在发散时间范围内的渐近正态性。该方法可应用于量化交易中的动态资产配置和投资组合优化，通过历史数据推断最优值，生成更稳健的交易信号。

title: Near Minimax Rates for Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
summary: In this paper, we study quantile distributional policy evaluation, where the return distribution under a given policy is approximated by the quantile Bellman fixed point $\bm\eta_m$. We investigate the statistical accuracy of estimating $\bm\eta_m$ across quantile resolutions under Wasserstein distances. Assuming access to a generative model, we construct a quantile fixed point estimator $\bm\eta_m^{(n)}$ from an empirical Markov decision process of $n$ observations per state-action pair and establish non-asymptotic error bounds under Wasserstein distances. When reward densities are uniformly bounded away from zero, we obtain a root-$n$ high-probability bound simultaneously over all resolutions $m$ and all Wasserstein orders $1\le p\le\infty$. When reward densities vanish at the support endpoints, we show that continuity and endpoint monotonicity suffice to preserve the same resolution-independent rate for $1\le p\le2$. For $p>2$, we establish a root-$n$ bound with coefficient $m^{1/2-1/p}$, together with a slower, resolution-independent $n^{-1/p}$ bound for every finite $p>2$. We further obtain resolution-independent $W_\infty$ consistency governed by the continuity modulus of reward quantile functions. To investigate the sharpness of these bounds, we characterize the exact local asymptotic minimax risk at each fixed resolution as the expected Wasserstein-coordinate norm of the efficient Gaussian limit and prove that our estimator attains it. We then examine the resolution dependence of this optimal local risk. A regular one-state instance has resolution-independent local risk constants, whereas a single endpoint-vanishing two-state instance exhibits growth of order $m^{1/2-1/p}$, up to logarithmic factors along a resolution subsequence, for every $p>2$.
core_methodology: Quantile distributional reinforcement learning for policy evaluation, focusing on statistical accuracy of estimating return distributions under Wasserstein distances.
